item.title: 'A complete surprise' - XDS-Astana respond to Harold Tejada biological passport abnormalities
item.author: Katy Madgwick
item.content:encoded: XDS-Astana have responded to the news that Harold Tejada is under investigation by the International Testing Agency (ITA), following suspected abnormalities in his biological passport. It was revealed on Friday, November 27, that Netcompany-Ineos had terminated their contract with Tejada following the news that the 29-year-old from Colombia had been notified of an anti-doping rule violation over the alleged use of a prohibited substance or method, following unexplained abnormalities in his biological passport.Tejada enjoyed success in 2026 at Paris-Nice, winning stage 6, and was second in a stage at the Tour de France, before recording a top-10 finish at the Vuelta a España later in the summer.He was due to transfer from XDS-Astana to Netcompany-Ineos in January 2027. He remains under contract with XDS-Astana until December 31. “This came as a complete surprise to the team,” XDS Astana said in a statement also issued on Friday, November 27.“In accordance with the disciplinary procedure before the ITA/UCI, the rider will be given an opportunity to present his defense and/or to accept the violation and a sanction. The team is not part of these proceedings. It is now for the relevant authorities to assess the case.“The team has a zero-tolerance policy with respect to doping practices, and it supports the UCI/ITA efforts to fight against doping in the sport of cycling.”Astana confirmed that Tejada had been suspended from the team, effective immediately.Tejada has spent his entire professional career at the Kazakh team, turning pro with them in 2020 and remaining for some seven seasons. His results gradually improved, from a stage win at the 2019 Tour de l'Avenir, which underscored his considerable climbing potential, to a victory on home soil at the 2024 Tour of Colombia, and finally his first WorldTour stage win at the 2026 Paris-Nice. Tejada released a statement on Friday, maintaining his innocence and stating his intention to cooperate with the investigation process. "From day one, I have acted with diligence and responsibility, providing all requested information in a timely manner. I will continue to do so throughout the entire process, with full respect for the anti-doping authorities and cycling institutions."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
item.author: Andrew Cunningham
item.content:encoded: Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven't been immune. That's why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years ago. "New thing, better features, same price" used to be a reliable formula, but now you're lucky if you can get the same thing for barely more than before.The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year's $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you're choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models.The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic.

item.title: Wahoo Black Friday deals 2026: All the day two discounts on Kickr trainers, Elemnt computers and more
item.author: josh.croxton@futurenet.com (Josh Croxton)
item.content:encoded: Welcome welcome one and all to the second day of the Black Friday sales (or the 32nd day if you look at it that way, given some retailers began talking about it in October). We're officially in the thick of the Black Friday bike deals weekend now, and there are dozens of solid Black Friday Wahoo deals to peruse. Some of which more discounted than we've ever seen before. With that in mind though, Black Friday itself has now passed and although the discounts are still flowing, I don't expect anything will get any cheaper from here on in. There have already been plenty of good deals to shout about in the world of Wahoo. The Kickr Core 2, down from $549 / £499 to just $399 / £399, is proving very popular. The Kickr V6 at £649 is another, and the deals on the entire range of Elemnt computers are hard to resist too. We've rounded up the best of the best below, so have a scroll to see what we've unearthed. Remember though, no deal is a good deal if it doesn't get used, so don't just buy something because it's discounted. If you want to take it a step further, you can add on the Zwift Ride v2 smart frame too. This still uses the Kickr Core v2, but the frame replaces your bike, saving you the need to wheel it through your house. It's also more widely adjustable, so you can share it with others in the house. View DealWahoo is slowly branching out into running, and the Kickr Run is its first foray into treadmills. I've not used it, but the general consensus is that it's very good. View DealThis is a bit of an odd one, as Amazon says its retail price is 624.99. That's not true; it's actually $499.99. However, it's still a nice discount on the biggest model in Wahoo's GPS computer range. The price fell by another $50 for Black Friday, which has improved the overall deal. View DealIn our opinion, it's likely the best for most people. Great navigation, great features, and very user friendly. View DealThis one's the smallest model in the range. It's perhaps more of a racer's choice, but it also packs more or less all the features of the Roam into a smaller package.That means it's cheaper still, but the smaller screen can be limiting in some cases. View DealThis is the same as the product above, but with the Zwift Cog and Click add-on, which replaces the cassette with a single-speed cog that's compatible with all modern groupsets. The 'Click' then lets you shift virtually in-game, which is silent, unlike the loud clunk you sometimes get from a derailleur. View DealThe Zwift Ride V2, paired with Kickr Core 2, is the whole-bike indoor solution, saving your own bike from the wear and tear. Its broad adjustability also means you can share it with others in your home, or try out new positions without changing the fit on your main bike.View DealIf you want to go even more premium than the Zwift Ride and Kickr Core pairing, this Kickr Bike Pro is it. It's broadly adjustable, tilts back and forth to mimic gradients, it's belt-driven so operation is virtually silent, and shifting is silent too. View DealOr a halfway house between the two, the Kickr Bike Shift, which offers the quiet operation and broad adjustability, but foregoes the tilting and a few other features to keep the price down. View DealWahoo is primarily a cycling-focussed company, but it's slowly branching out into running, and this Kickr Run is its first foray into treadmills. View DealThe Kickr Climb lets you simulate gradients of up to 20%, by literally lifting the front of your bike up and down, to make things feel all the more realistic. It's a useful addition to your setup if you're trying to train for riding up long climbs and you want to mimic the position. View DealThe Roam barely needs an introduction. It's the goldilocks GPS in Wahoo's range, balancing price, screen size and battery life nicely. View DealThis one's the baby of the range. More of a racer's choice, but it also packs more or less all the features of the Roam into a smaller, cheaper package.View DealAnd finally, if you want the biggest screen possible for your bike computer then it has to be the Elemnt Ace. It's really very large, the battery is bigger, but of course, so is the price. View DealYou can easily make do with a simple fan for indoor training, but if you want to have a better time you can get a smart fan like the Kickr Headwind. It'll either work as a dumb fan (just turn it up and down as needed) or you can set it to increase power in line with your heart rate monitor, so it'll blow stronger the harder you ride. View DealOur other Black Friday 2026 roundups👕 : With 25% off sitewide, we've rounded up our favourite items from the British brand.💾 : A live, ever-changing roundup of our favourite deals on Garmin's bike computers, smartwatches, heart rate monitors and more, from Garmin's own site and beyond.

item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 11/28/26
item.author: Jake Devin
item.content:encoded: We’re easing towards the end of the Thanksgiving break, and closer and closer to a lockout-shaped break imposed by MLB owners. We’ll see if the league has one last offseason frenzy in it before things go dark. We saw a flurry ahead of Thanksgiving last week, and with the CBA set to expire on December 1st, it’s fair to wonder if we’ll get another surge to the finish line. Such a surge may have begun last night, the Blue Jays firing the hot stove up again last night to ink Jazz Chisholm Jr. to a one-year deal worth $20 million. That marks the official end of Chisholm’s Yankee tenure, though it had been assumed for weeks that he’d be departing. The Yankees themselves have been quiet the last few days, though they seem poised to potentially make a major move. The Adrian Morejon sweepstakes appear ready to resolve, and ideally we’ll get a clearer picture of the shape of the Yankees’ offseason plan before the lights go off.1. At this point, what do you think Adrian Morejon’s eventual contract will end up at? In excess of $100MM?2. Weere you surprised to see Jazz Chisholm Jr. take what’s essentially a pillow contract?

item.title: Bezzecchi on pole, Marquez claims MotoGP qualifying title
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Aprilia MotoGP rider Marco Bezzecchi took a commanding pole position for the season finale in Valencia, but the retiring Marc Marquez took the 2026 qualifying title.MotoGP's qualifying championship BMW M Award scores riders by qualifying position using the same top-15 points system as for grand prix finishes, and awards a BMW car to the winner each year.Marquez was the winner seven consecutive times between 2013 and 2019, and then prevailed in 2025 before doubling up in what has now turned out to be his final season.Bezzecchi was the only rival who had a shot at denying him a ninth Award in the final round, but second place for Marquez was enough to keep him ahead in the standings - despite the gargantuan 0.463s gap between them.This came as Bezzecchi obliterated the MotoGP lap record at the track with a searing 1m27.844s.Raul Fernandez used three soft rear tyres in Q2 and briefly sat on provisional pole but ultimately ended up nearly six tenths behind Bezzecchi in third.Alex Marquez, Jorge Martin and Fabio Di Giannantonio made it a top six made up entirely of Aprilia and Ducati riders.Pedro Acosta was third of three KTM riders in Q2, beaten by Enea Bastianini (seventh), stand-in Pol Espargaro (eighth) and also potential 2027 Ducati team-mate Fermin Aldeguer (ninth).This was despite Espargaro crashing at Turn 1 late on shortly after setting his fastest lap (which he'd spent half of in Acosta's tow).Ai Ogura, who tumbled at Turn 11 at the end, and Joan Mir completed the Q2 order. Brad Binder was 0.029s away from a farewell Q2 appearance, losing out to Mir for the final Q1 transfer spot and settling for 13th on the grid - which means team-mate Acosta has maintained a perfect qualifying record versus his team-mates over the first three seasons of his MotoGP career.Ducati factory stand-in Iker Lecuona was 14th, just half a tenth off Q2, while Johann Zarco was likewise close in 15th - and compatriot Fabio Quartararo led the Yamaha contingent one spot lower.1 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) 1m27.844s2 Marc Marquez (Ducati) +0.463s3 Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.589s4 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) +0.736s5 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +0.795s6 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +0.851s7 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +0.936s8 Pol Espargaro (Tech3 KTM) +1.009s9 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +1.026s10 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +1.040s11 Ai Ogura (Trackhouse Aprilia) +1.306s12 Joan Mir (Honda) +1.572s13 Brad Binder (KTM) +0.029s to Q214 Iker Lecuona (Ducati) +0.056s15 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +0.082s16 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +0.203s17 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +0.231s18 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +0.380s19 Luca Marini (Honda) +0.419s20 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +0.436s21 Augusto Fernandez (Pramac Yamaha) +0.517s22 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +0.944s

item.title: Why Williams breached the 2025 F1 cost cap
Wout van Aert to make cyclo-cross return in Antwerp, with World Championships tilt on the cards
item.author: Katy Madgwick
item.content:encoded: Wout van Aert has confirmed his return to the cyclo-cross field for the 2026-2027 season, with the likely aim of representing Belgium at the UCI World Championships in Ostend in January.According to Flemish newspaper , the Visma-Lease a Bike rider will make his debut on December 19 in Antwerp, the same place where he began his campaign last season, finishing 7th on the day.Van Aert raced a reduced calendar of six races in 2025-2026 and, despite two second-place finishes, was unable to record a win in the discipline for the first time since his debut season in 2010. He was set to race eight races in total but an ankle fracture sustained in Mol in early January forced an early end to his winter programme. This season he looks set to expand his off-road schedule, with the suggestion that he may race around 12 races, with the first indication that these will include the World Championships in Ostend on January 31, 2027, an outcome which Belgian national coach Angelo De Clercq had previously suggested was uncertain.It's still a relatively late start for Van Aert, as hopes for a potential debut at the Superprestige series in Ruddervoorde were quashed by confirmation that the Belgian would attend Visma-Lease a Bike's Spanish training camp in early December.While his exact race programme is yet to be determined, it looks increasingly likely that Van Aert will take aim at the world title in January. He had already confirmed he would opt out of the most recent edition in Hulst in 2026 prior to his ankle injury, moving on from the mud to targets on the road, with the Spring Classics his first major goals of the season. This season could mark a return to Worlds for a tilt at a rainbow jersey that he won three years in a row, from 2016-2018. His three most recent attempts to repeat the feat have resulted in second-place finishes to his long-time rival, Mathieu van der Poel, including in Ostend in 2021. It's currently unclear whether or not the Dutchman intends to race off-road this winter.As for Van Aert, the 32-year-old has reduced his participation in the off-road discipline where he made his name in recent seasons; however, he continues to include cyclocross as part of his schedule, racing every season since his junior debut in 2010. This season marks his 17th consecutive winter as an elite cyclo-cross rider.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: The hill I will die on: Cheques are still the best way to pay for things | Claire Jackson
item.author: Claire Jackson
item.content:encoded: A debit card might be quicker and easier, but there are thrills big and small to be had from whipping out your chequebookIt often takes other people to identify your quirks. Mine is writing cheques, a fact I was made aware of recently by a younger colleague, who watched with bemusement as I filled one out. He’d never seen a chequebook in the wild, he explained, with the air of a naturalist encountering a rare species. He looked on as I, a millennial, wrote “one hundred and forty-one pounds and thirty pence only”, that last word thrilling in its assertiveness – I will pay my bill, South East Water, and not a penny more!Having examined the whole procedure, including my procuring a stamp and envelope to send it off, he concluded – as so many have – that the process would be far better executed online. A friend also politely fed back that, although she appreciates how I “enclose a cheque” in every birthday card to her daughter, could I perhaps just do a bank transfer like everyone else?Claire Jackson is a journalist who writes about classical music, art and animalsContinue reading...

If you bought a set yesterday then that's the luck of the draw to some degree but maybe you can whinge to customer service (politely, or there'll be trouble) or something at Sigma Sports; the squeaky wheel gets the oil, so they say.Yes, you read that right... you'll SAVE £1,260. Madness.November 28, 2026 – 5:09 AMHere's a deal I actually bought this time last year for a family member with a similar discount.Well made, from a VERY trusted brand so you can be sure that when you're working on your bike you're not actually damaging it and risking disaster. Not a sexy buy. but you'll end up using it all the time if you look after your own bikes. If memory serves it does not come with bits (3/8" ones), so you'll have to sort those out to suit your needs, but it does mean you can tailor your kit to your bike - no point having a T25 if you don't need one.November 28, 2026 – 5:17 AM15% off the saddle I use on every test bike I can? Oh go on then!Look, saddles are a personal choice, and I'm not saying this will definitely suit you, but I love it to bits to the point that when it got replaced by a new model I asked Selle Italia if I could have any of the old stock. They said no, so I guess I have to consider putting my money where my mouth is and just buying more...November 28, 2026 – 5:21 AMThis one is DEEPLY boring but also REALLY important...If you let your cleats get really worn before replacing them (as we all do, let's be honest) then you are increasing your risk of injury as your foot position changes away from the ideal position. Also when they're really worn they can just more horrible to clip in with.November 28, 2026 – 5:29 AMA couple of very tasty lights from Knog on offer. I used the old version of the rear light and loved it; it's got a curved bank of LEDs that means extremely good side visibility, which in tern means you're less likely to get squished by a taxi. November 28, 2026 – 5:51 AMAs someone who rides most places I have to lock my bike up all the time. If you want to protect your pride and joy, then Amazon has a bumper sale on Kryptonite locks.Not to be leaning hard on the scare tactics but bike thefts are on the rise, especially for ebikes. if you've a high value machine then it makes sense to protect it with something like the New York Diamond, a D-lock that takes 10 angle discs to break through, which is enough of a deterrent even if it wasn't giant, yellow, and heavy.November 28, 2026 – 5:56 AMEndura BaaBaa socks are a classic of the winter wardrobe - I've just put mine in the wash after an absolute drenching. They're not the absolute best, but for £7.79 you can't really go wrong for merino riding socks. Mine have held up extremely well over a couple of winters hard use, so I'm happy to recommend them. November 28, 2026 – 6:40 AMI've had a set of these Castelli neoprene gloves for going on 15 years now and they're still going strong. If you've got XXL hands then they're an absolute bargain right now for $25 at Competitive Cyclist.November 28, 2026 – 6:49 AMHow about 30% off Oakley Sutros? Beloved of Mathieu van der Poel (and me, but that's maybe less impressive) they give excellent coverage, they're comfy, and they look cool. Also the best option, the one with a Prizm Road lens, is the one discounted, so unless you need the all god version then follow my advice. November 28, 2026 – 6:58 AMI don't use gels (sponsor me, Haribo!), and I have no idea if these are good or not, or tasty. I think you should buy them mostly because Laini Ritsch Multer aka Laini Bones is the CFO of the company and is an absolute hoot on Instagram, and my girlfriend and I want to be friends with her and I think this is the only way I can facilitate that. Laini, if you ever want to come take some transatlantic Strava crowns there are plenty over here.November 28, 2026 – 7:37 AMBonjour folks. Here's one that's got my finger hovering over the buy-now button. It's something that is either quite uncommon in many a cyclist's toolbox and I'm about to blow your mind (pun not intended), or they've somehow passed me by and I'm just being old-news Josh again. Either way, on the hope that it's the former, allow me to introduce the humble precision air blaster. A tool that, quite simply, blows a jet of high-speed air to a very specific location, using a handheld device no bigger than a stapler. My introduction to these things - not necessarily this Muc-Off version, but the technology as a whole - was a couple of years ago at a gravel race, where, after our recon ride and subsequent bike wash the day before the race, a friend used one to blast water off his drivetrain, so that it wouldn't rust overnight. A brilliant little hack that not only did a better job than a rag, but did it much more quickly, and tidily too. There are cheaper versions on Amazon, but given I've not used any of the ones currently on sale, I don't know whether they'll last five minutes. I've heard good things about this Muc-Off version though, and now it's half price!View Deal

item.title: Pedrosa leaves KTM MotoGP project
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: KTM's long-serving test rider Dani Pedrosa has exited his role.The now-41-year-old had joined KTM back in 2018 at the conclusion of his storied career in full-time grand prix racing competition.He was a marquee signing for KTM, well-regarded for his feedback and feel but also specifically in being lured away from arch-rival manufacturer Honda.Some notably competitive wildcard outings followed for Pedrosa on the KTM, and he also helped refine a KTM RC16 that at one point had the reputation of being perhaps MotoGP's most recalcitrant machine.But eventually Pedrosa stepped away from wildcards entirely and also stepped into more of a secondary tester role, emphasising work on rideability while new tester Pol Espargaro became the focal point for performance work.And with KTM's new 850cc bike for the 2027 regulations now being readied for its debut, Pedrosa - who has also earned acclaim as a TV pundit for Spanish broadcaster DAZN - is ceasing his participation in the KTM project.KTM motorsport boss Pit Beirer said KTM "can only thank" Pedrosa "for his expertise and passion" and that he "helped us make big steps forward for the project"."His work with the likes of Mika [Kallio] and Pol and the whole test team pushed us to be where we are today, and his talent was always obvious: we could see this from the times he excited us with his wildcards."

item.title: Hankook's bid for F1 tyre supply - what you need to know
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Hankook has begun a Formula 1 tyre testing programme and opened talks with teams as it prepares to bid on becoming grand prix racing’s official supplier from 2029, The Race has learned.F1’s current contract with Pirelli runs until the end of 2028, after the Italian company won F1’s most recent tender deal, which covered the period from 2025-2027, against a rival bid from Bridgestone. Its contract was extended by a further season in June this year after an option was taken up by the FIA.From 2029, however, a new tender process is set to be launched by the FIA and there looks set to be fresh competition to secure the right to be the official F1 supplier.It is understood that Pirelli wants to wait to see details of the tender before deciding if it enters the fray to extend its current spell which stretches back to 2011, while Bridgestone has long evaluated an F1 return with representatives having attended races.However, it has now emerged that Hankook is ready to throw its hat into the ring too and has been secretly ramping up its own efforts.Representatives of the company were spotted at the recent Las Vegas Grand Prix, which was understood to have been their second visit to an F1 race this year following a trip to Madrid in September.The Race understands that Hankook has used these trips to meet a majority of teams and discuss plans with bosses, CEOs and other senior executives.The trips to races, which also included visits to events in China, Japan and Singapore in 2025, are only one side of its efforts to get ready for 2029, however.It is understood that Hankook has already committed a 44-person task force within the company to prepare for an F1 entry.Beyond committing research and development capability plus simulator running, it has this year completed two development tests for F1 rubber using a modified F2-equivalent-mule car to evaluate potential construction as well as different compounds.A third test has been scheduled to work on its wet-weather rubber, which it hopes can also help it develop a tyre that features a narrower spray plume to reduce visibility problems caused in wet conditions.Hankook is also working hard on production and manufacturing planning that would be required to supply F1, F2 and F3 tyres that would come under the umbrella of any tyre tender contract.Hankook is certainly no stranger to FIA competition, with the South Korean company already the official tyre supplier to the World Rally Championship and has just ended its supply to Formula E where Bridgestone is taking over for the upcoming season. Earlier this year Hankook was also named as a global partner of the governing body.The period of the new F1 tyre tender beyond 2029 will almost certainly cover the transition to the next rules era, with F1 setting sights on new lighter and nimbler cars to coincide with the switch to V8 power units from 2030.The plans are also set to include a new tyre design, which is set to reduce wheel size slightly from the current 18-inch design.

item.title: Grand Theft Anthropic: how GTA can inspire a fightback against AI | Alexander Hurst
item.author: Alexander Hurst
item.content:encoded: Tech billionaires are taking us for a ride. But new ‘poison pill’ software could help shield human-made creative output from hijacking Grand Theft Auto VI came out on the same day that Anthropic made its stock market debut. I keep thinking about that coincidence. As more than one tech writer has pointed out, the new GTA took 13 years to make, more than $1bn of investment and involved 9,000 sets of human hands, and it will probably be the last blockbuster video game to be fully free of generative AI.On the day of its release, a group chat with my most gaming-minded male friends erupted in discussion about whether or not video games, and GTA VI specifically, rose to the level of art. Exploring a national park? Yes, that’s there. Badly assemble a coffee table from “Krapea” (the game’s fictional furniture company)? Ditto. Eating a hot dog? Why not. All of it gloriously human in origin. Perhaps that in itself is an argument for how GTA VI crosses the blurry line from entertainment to something more. It is a medium by which human beings offer others a (necessarily incomplete) interpretation of what it’s like to be them in the world, or to try to transcend it.Alexander Hurst writes for Guardian Europe from ParisContinue reading...

item.title: Yankees news: Black Friday Shopping
item.author: John Griffin
item.content:encoded: MLB Trade Rumors | Mark Polishuk: Ever since the trade deadline, the Yankees have made it very clear that they have wanted to add to their catching contingent, looking for a right-handed bat to go alongside the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. With San Diego looking to clear a path to playing time for top prospect Ethan Salas, two names that the Yankees have been looking into are Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin. While both are right-handed hitters, their profiles are remarkably different: Fermin would give the Yankees one of the best defensive tandems in the game, and Campusano would provide some power behind the dish the team has desperately needed in recent years. For what it’s worth, not only have the two teams made some high-profile moves in recent years, the situation very much mimics the 2023-2024 winter: the Padres need rotation help, the Yankees have an excess of starters, and the Padres have exactly what the Yankees need.ESPN | Jorge Castillo: As Andrew detailed for us yesterday, former Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. agreed to a one-year contract with the Toronto Blue Jays that contains both a player and a team option for 2028 and which guarantees him $34.5 million. The move brings to a close a dramatic Yankees career for the 28-year-old infielder, which saw him provide a spark to a scuffling 2024 squad and become a key contributor at the hot corner as the team went to the World Series for the first time since 2009, fill a critical role in the middle of the order in 2025, before scuffling in his contract year while courting controversy on and off the field.MLB Trade Rumors | Darragh McDonald: As Friday came to a close, we learned that another multi-year Yankee who hit free agency would not be returning in 2027. Steady long man Ryan Yarbrough is signing with the Cubs, per Robert Murray of FanSided (who also broke the Chisholm news). The Yankees’ decision to sign Brent Suter essentially rendered Yarbrough’s possible future with the team redundant, as Suter has a similar profile and better stuff. Between Suter, Brent Headrick, and Tim Hill, the bullpen was getting fairly left-handed regardless. The Athletic | Jayson Stark: (subscription required) Following Tarik Skubal’s record-breaking nine-year, $450 million megacontract with the New York Mets, Jayson Stark of decided to rank the best and worst free agent contracts ( extensions) signed by pitchers over the years. Perhaps unsurprisingly, two of the five best belong to the Yankees: CC Sabathia, who led the Yankees to the 2009 World Series in the first year of his deal, and Gerrit Cole, who has won one Cy Young and finished as the runner-up one other time over the first seven years of his deal.

item.title: What Happened to JFK-Era Intel Records?
item.content:encoded: Fifty years after John F. Kennedy's assassination, Disclosure podcast's Jason Leopold requested the US Defense Intelligence Agency's daily briefings for the surrounding two months, a potential trove of details about foreign governments' contemporary planning and reactions. Twelve years later, he received a response -- three days' worth of briefings, with redactions, 41 pages in all. Jason and co-host Matt Topic delve into the secrecy surrounding the Kennedy-era records, what has become of nearly two months' worth of briefings and what could have led to the destruction of intelligence reports from a pivotal moment in US history. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The M5 MacBook Air just got its biggest discount since Apple raised the price
item.author: Sheena Vasani
item.content:encoded: If you’ve been holding off on buying a new MacBook Air since Apple raised prices by $200 in June, you’re in luck. The 13-inch is on sale at Amazon and Best Buy with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage starting at $999 ($300 off) for Black Friday, which is the lowest price we’ve seen since the hike. If you want a larger display, Amazon and Best Buy are also taking $300 off the otherwise identical 15-inch model with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, dropping it to $1,199.The M5-equipped MacBook Air is a good middle ground if you need more power than the MacBook Neo — which, thanks to a $100 discount, is $599 — but don’t want to splurge on a MacBook Pro. Its faster chip, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage make it better suited for multitasking and creative work in apps like Photoshop and Premiere. You also get a higher-resolution display, better speakers, a backlit keyboard that makes typing in the dark easier, and faster ports. Plus, its sharper webcam supports Apple’s Center Stage feature, which automatically adjusts the framing to keep you in view during video calls.Of course, the Air can’t match the performance or higher-end displays you can get with a MacBook Pro, whether you opt for an M5 model, the newer M5 Pro model with a PROLED XDR Display, or one of the M6-powered machines. A Pro may be worth the extra money if you regularly edit video or work on more demanding creative projects. But if you mostly need a laptop for work, browsing, and occasional photo or video editing, the M5 Air is more than capable.

item.title: Heat 108, Knicks 105: “Really tough to win a poorly coached, corruptly reffed, half rotation injured game.”
item.author: Russell Richardson
item.content:encoded: The Knicks (12-7) lost two Emirates NBA Cup games this season but defeated the Cavaliers on Wednesday. Their chances of reaching the next round and continuing their defense of the Cup weren’t nonexistent, but they needed to beat the Heat (11-7) by more than six points and for the Pacers to drop the Sixers.First things first: the surging Heat are a handful even when New York’s roster is complete. The Knicks had to meet the challenge without OG Anunoby (calf), Andre Drummond (concussion), Miles McBride (groin), and Jordan Clarkson (foot). The remaining players weren’t altogether healthy, either: Karl-Anthony Towns (19 PTS, 10 RBS, 34 MIN) has an abdominal contusion, and Josh Hart (6 PTS, 9 RBS, 8 AST) is playing through a sore knee and shoulder. Our depleted Knickerbockers fell behind in the first quarter, then went down by 23 in the second. They cut their deficit to five in the third frame and had the Heat on the ropes in crunch time. A few missed free throws, an uncalled flagrant foul, and odd coaching decisions let the rally—and their Cup dreams—slip through their fingers. Final score: 108-105.Quoth DWLLTheKnicksfan: “Really tough to win a poorly coached, corruptly reffed, half rotation injured game. Respect that it was close.”After the Knicks fell behind 15-7, coach Mike Brown replaced Hart with Pacôme Dadiet (4 PTS, 1 STL, 21 MIN, +7). Pac-Man played arm-flapping defense that disrupted the flow and led to a Miami turnover, then dunked a Brunson pass on the run. We’re starting to see the vision! The French fella stayed on the floor when the next round of swaps came, playing alongside Brunson, Hart, Jose Alvarado (7 PTS, 15 MIN), and James Wiseman (11 PTS). The latter lasted just two minutes and committed a foul that heralded the return of Towns. Not a great first look on a night when Drummond was out.New York logged nine boards in the first quarter. Giannis Antetokounmpo (22 PTS, 23 RBS, 32 MIN) matched that total alone, scarfing up most of Miami’s 14 boards. A physical game had Towns wincing in pain, and we were wincing at New York’s crappy shooting (2-of-11 from deep). With the Floridians sinking half of their three-pointers, the Knicks trailed 31-21 at the break.In the second quarter, Mohamed Diawara and the Tylers (Kolek, Nickel) took the floor. Miami scored 12 unanswered while the ’Bockers continued to shoot like the Blind Boys of Alabama. The rookie Nickel looked lost and the coach bewildered. Mike Brown called for time when the score reached 48-27.Out of that timeout, Brown sent Wiseman and Dadiet back in. Wiseman’s minutes were rough. On consecutive plays, Wiggins picked off his inbound pass for a layup, and then Ryan Conwell intercepted his inbound pass. Unsurprisingly, he suffered a quick hook. Mike was running out of levers to pull as his team fell behind by 23. With four rotation players out and his starters all posting a plus-minus of -13 or worse, the coach fielded 11 different players in the first half in an attempt to slow Erik Spoelstra’s squad, which scored inside, outside, and wherever else it wanted.Thanks to a spirited late-half nine-oh run, the home team entered halftime trailing 60-44. There was plenty of blame to go around for our heroes. Towns (still painin’!) and Brunson combined for 25 of their team’s 44 points, but the other starters had five points each, and the Knicks’ bench had been outscored by its Miami counterpart, 30-4.Through the half, the Flamingos shot 45% from the field and 36% from deep (9-of-25), while New York managed 40% and a miserable 21% (4-of-19). The Heat held only slight advantages in rebounds (24-23) and points in the paint (22-18) but were considerably better at protecting the ball. Nine Knicks turnovers yielded 11 Miami points, while the Heat committed just four turnovers that yielded three New York points. Worse, Miami won the battle for second-chance points, 10-0.Over the first two minutes of the second half, Towns, Bridges, and Shamet combined for nine points to cut the deficit to 61-53. Miami fought back, but New York looked rejuvenated and alert (a marked improvement from the tryptophan blues of the first half). By the midway point of the quarter, the Knicks had converted five straight shots, reducing their deficit to five. As we’ve seen in game after game this season, it takes a lot of energy to climb out of deep holes. As the Knicks faltered, back-to-back Bridges turnovers allowed Giannis and Bam Adebayo (25 PTS, 7 RBS) to hammer Miami’s lead back to 11.Our heroes got an unexpected lift from Wiseman. He leaped into the fray, scoring seven points on three buckets and a free throw late in the third. That was more like it! Add a Brunson floater and an Antetokounmpo shot-clock violation, and New York trailed 86-79 at the horn.Bam was a bother to start the fourth, netting two buckets, blocking shots by Shamet and Kolek, and drawing two fouls from Towns. Towns headed to the bench with four fouls at the 8:27 mark. Meanwhile, Shamet, Bridges, and Kolek each contributed layups to keep the Knicks within striking distance. The Heat struggled from the perimeter, with OAKAAKUYOAKs Tim Hardaway Jr. and Bobby Portis blowing opportunities to extend the lead.Down 91-85 with plenty of game remaining, New York scored seven unanswered points, fueled by the bench mob. Wednesday’s hero, Alvarado, scored five consecutive points, including a step-back three off his own offensive rebound, while Dadiet contributed a steal and a reverse layup off Brunson’s eighth assist to give the Knicks their first lead. Davion Mitchell finally broke Miami’s scoring drought with a floater, putting the Heat ahead 93-92 with six minutes remaining.At the two-minute mark, the good guys trailed by three points after two freebies by Shamet. From there, Giannis launched an ill-advised, deep airball late in the shot clock; Brunson and Pelle Larsson traded free throws; Hart made one of two at the stripe; and Adebayo made the differential four with 44 seconds left. Captain Clutch’s floater made it 104-102. Giannis missed two free throws with 14 seconds on the clock, and Adebayo fouled Wiseman on the loose ball, giving our heroes a of hope. My bingo card did not have Wiseman shooting free throws with the game on the line. How about yours?The young journeyman made one, missed one, and Giannis snagged the board and called a timeout. 104-103, 13 seconds to go. When play resumed, Dadiet fouled Mitchell, who made both attempts. On the Knicks’ inbounds play, the ball swung to Brunson in the corner, where he was fouled by Conwell. Even though Conwell violated JB’s landing space, Scott “The Enforcer” Foster deemed it a common foul. Cap made two of three at the line. Spoelstra called a timeout. 106-105, nine seconds.Larsson got a breakaway dunk—on the exact same inbounds play the Heat had run on their previous possession. Mike Brown elected not to call a timeout, and Brunson missed a contested triple to end the game.This is your recap, chaps. As for the Knicks, they’ll sleep in their own beds for a few more days and host the Hawks on Sunday. Rest up, troops.

item.title: The best Black Friday deals you can still get on AirPods, Macs, and other Apple gear
item.author: Brad Bourque, Sheena Vasani
item.content:encoded: Black Friday is entering the evening, which means one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch is coming to a close. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts still apply to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro, too, which are available at their lowest prices to date.In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers.Earbud and headphone dealsYou can buy the on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review.The are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is $19 shy of their best price to date (Target also has them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review.If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the are on sale starting at $79.99 ($120 off) at Amazon and Target — a new low price. The headphones are a noticeable improvement over their predecessor, delivering more detailed sound and support for lossless audio. They also last up to 50 hours on a single charge, while their memory foam ear cushions make them comfortable enough for long listening sessions. Read our review.The are down to around $89.95 ($80 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, nearly matching their lowest price to date. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. They’re also exceptionally comfortable, with four ear tip sizes to help you find a secure fit. Sure, you don’t get wireless charging, but they offer IPX4 water resistance and up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Read our review.The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,099 ($300 off) — a new low price — at Amazon. The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review.The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,749 ($250 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is a new low price. The Pro builds on its predecessor with a faster chip and support for Wi-Fi 7. In our testing, it handled multitasking, photo editing, and occasional video editing with ease while still delivering exceptional battery life. It lacks the newer MacBook Pro’s gorgeous OLED display, but its Mini LED screen still looks great, especially given its smooth 120Hz refresh rate. It also offers excellent speakers and a good selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot. Read our review.The is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration starting at $179 ($50 off) at Amazon and Walmart, matching its best price to date, while Best Buy is currently $20 higher. Apple’s newest entry-level smartwatch remains our top recommendation for anyone who wants a basic fitness tracker, as it offers all the essentials alongside an always-on display and Apple’s S10 chip, which enables on-device Siri requests. Read our review.AirTags, chargers, and other dealsYou can buy the with 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi on Amazon in select colors for $484 ($115 off), which is the best price we’ve seen since Apple’s recent price hikes. It has a smaller screen and a slower chip than the newer model, and it lacks an OLED screen, the Acoustic Display, and water resistance. Still, it’s a great option for reading and everyday use that’s currently more affordable than its $599 successor, with support for Apple Intelligence and the Apple Pencil Pro. Read our review.Apple’s latest Magic Mouse is matching its all-time low of $59.99 ($20 off) at Amazon. The wireless mouse features a touch-sensitive surface that lets you scroll through documents and swipe between apps with simple gestures; it also pairs automatically with compatible Macs and offers support for USB-C. Updated to reflect current pricing / availability and a newer deal on the Apple Pencil (USB-C).

item.title: Sony’s 1000XM4C headphones are a Black Friday bargain at $198
item.author: Cameron Faulkner
item.content:encoded: Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. The 2026 version, called the WH-1000XM4C, sounds nearly as good as the pricier XM6 model (currently $348), but is down to $198 during Black Friday at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. That’s $100 off their October launch price.There’s a reason why Sony went back to refine the XM4. Our former reviewer Chris Welch praised them for being super comfortable and for having close to perfect features for the price, especially compared to its successor, the XM3 (still my daily driver, for what it’s worth). The XM4s had better sound quality and noise cancellation, plus improved mics, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that can detect when you remove them to automatically pause audio. Now, with the XM4C, there are further improvements, most notably a 10-band equalizer in the app (compared to the original XM4’s five-band) that my colleague John Higgins says really helped the headphones’ midrange frequencies open up.These are a great buy, but they aren’t your only Sony headphones deal to consider right now. are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027.

item.title: Mercedes' early advantage is even scarier than it looks
item.author: Josh Suttill
item.content:encoded: Mercedes has been the benchmark 2026 team, but given it’s only won one of the last six races, what’s behind its dominant start to Formula 1’s Qatar Grand Prix weekend? World champion Kimi Antonelli led a Mercedes one-two in both practice sessions, four and a half tenths clear of the nearest competition on single-lap pace in FP2 - despite their fastest laps being set on mediums.Reading into the final classification is a messy endeavour given two red flags disrupted run plans but it actually makes Mercedes’ position even more formidable.Russell got very close to completing a full lap on softs but did not finish the lap in time - still, his theoretical fastest lap (taking the two sectors he did do on the faster tyre) was some 0.835 seconds faster than the quickest non-Mercedes, Max Verstappen’s Red Bull.Theoretical best laps FP2 Russell 1m22.683sVerstappen +0.835sPiastri +0.866sHamilton +1.284sMercedes’ advantage was also sizeable when looking at the adjusted long-run pace in FP2. You can slice such analysis multiple ways but accounting for laps in traffic as best as possible Antonelli leads the way, a whopping 0.810 seconds faster per lap than Verstappen's Red Bull. Antonelli (Mercedes) 1m28.074sRussell (Mercedes) +0.205sVerstappen (Red Bull) +0.810sHadjar (Red Bull) +1.058sNorris (McLaren) +1.061sPiastri (McLaren) +1.173s*Ferrari didn’t complete a representative long runMercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin called it “one of our better Fridays this year” while deputy Mercedes team boss Bradley Lord said Mercedes “hit the ground running” as the car “seems to suit this circuit”.Lord said there were “very minimal differences” between Antonelli and Russell’s set-ups by the end of the day, with them looking closely matched over both single laps and longer runs. Russell had made some, in his words, “good changes” after FP1 that made him comfortable with the balance. Lord said the car is “competitive in both the high speed and the low speed. One of the question marks we had was the low-speed performance with the new update [introduced in Malaysia].“Obviously, this circuit bias is towards the medium and high speed where we know we've definitely made gains.“So we're making good use of that. Then hopefully it just reflects our ongoing learning about how to get the most out of the car with this package on it.” So there is an element of Qatar playing to the strengths of the package and nullifying the effect of the Malaysia upgrade having put the car in a narrower performance window, for low-speed corners in particular - even if Mercedes has made gains since then in widening it. There are far fewer heavy braking zones or tricky corner entries like Mexico, where the W17 struggled more. The Mercedes drivers, by and large, avoided the balance issues that have been plaguing rivals like Red Bull in Qatar. “They find the key to fix this balance, and this balance issue we can have here by having a massive front limitation in high-speed, medium-speed corners, without compromising the entry,” Red Bull’s technical director Pierre Wache observed. “They are able to do that, and we have the work to do to achieve better.” Plus, the cars are fairly energy-starved in Qatar - particularly through the high-speed corners and main straight - so the efficiency of Mercedes’ energy management package is rewarded here, as it was in Monza and Baku. But the fact it still has a significant advantage over McLaren (with that same power unit) and Red Bull (also with a very strong power unit) suggests it has a lot to do with Mercedes’s strength in high-speed corners and it finding a strong car balance that its rivals can’t. Where Red Bull and McLaren are strugglingMax Verstappen has won four of the last six races, but he was struggling with some familiar problems with his RB22.He suffered team radio issues early in FP1 that were later resolved, but a “disconnected” balance problem remained throughout Friday. “It's quite a unique track. It's not an easy track to get things right, so I hope we can do a little bit better,” Verstappen said. “The gap to Mercedes is very big, so we need a big jump for that. But I think already from our side, if we can get that balance more together, that's probably already half of the laptime that we're losing.” Verstappen also complained of “heavy steering” in FP2 with Wache admitting, “The car is struggling here a lot in terms of kerbing and stuff that will damage. We have to fix that.” McLaren’s also wary of the fragility of its car as it started the day on its older specification of floor before switching the drivers onto the new floor introduced in Las Vegas. “Many people can run off and damage parts, so we just made sure that we didn't damage any of the new spec for this car,” McLaren’s senior racing director Randy Singh explained. McLaren’s power unit exploitation deficit to Mercedes and known baked-in 2026 missteps like short gear ratios explain some of its gap to Mercedes, who Norris said are “just a different level compared to everyone this weekend”. “It shows just in general how far off we are. “It's not like something works better for them here. I mean, you can just clearly see if they're quick here, they're quick in a lot of other places for the same reason. “So I think it's more a realisation of where we stand relative to them.” The time loss is most visible on the run to Turn 1, where Norris tops out at 322km/h compared to Antonelli’s 332km/h and has already lost 0.175s by the exit of that corner. It’s also present in the high-speed corners at Turn 12-15 where Norris loses another 0.125s, as the more planted Mercedes stretches its legs. The Red Bull ends up leaking even more time there as Verstappen loses over three tenths there alone to Antonelli. Mercedes has its eye on Red Bull as the “next team”, but Lord said he wouldn’t be surprised to see a five or six-car battle for pole position on Saturday.There’s clearly one front-running team at risk of being excluded from that fight in Qatar. What happened to ‘outlier’ Ferrari? The outlier among the top teams on Friday was Ferrari as its drivers didn’t even manage to complete a representative long-run in FP2. Charles Leclerc spun while Lewis Hamilton stopped on-track with a power unit problem. “It's been just a very, very difficult session,” Leclerc admitted after FP2. “When I lost the car, it probably made it even worse, so we just decided to change the floor, which cost us quite a bit of time. “But to be honest, this is not even the reason why we were slow. We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2, and it's very difficult to understand what is the outlier. “I think not only for us but for everybody, particularly comparing to Mercedes, that seems to be, they always kind of had the best car, but now it's to an extent that we did not expect.” As you can see from a comparison of their fastest FP2 laps, Leclerc’s laptime bleed to Antonelli is consistent throughout the lap.And even on their fastest theoretical laps, there’s major losses in all three of his best sectors - 0.570s in sector one, 0.443s in sector two and 0.484s in sector three. That’s likely to lead to a long night of head-scratching from Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren as to why Mercedes appears to be in a different league in Qatar and whether there’s any chance of anyone catching it.

item.title: The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
item.author: Sheena Vasani
item.content:encoded: We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date.The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game.The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify.

item.title: 'It's always sour to lose' admits Tibor Del Grosso after going second to Thibau Nys in Ostrava at World Cup opener
item.author: Ben Goddard
item.content:encoded: The 23-year-old was battling for victory on the last lap with rival Thibau Nys (Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions), but came out second best in the first duel of the season between the pair.Del Grosso said that he felt ‘sour’ losing to his Belgian rival after conceding the lead and failing to regain the front position in the snow during the final corners, while Nys stayed on the firmer ground.“I don't think it was a bad performance, if you're close to winning. Of course, it's always sour to lose,” said Del Grosso afterwards to organisers.“It was just a matter of having the lead and keeping the lead going into the last corner, at some point Thibau [Nys] came with quite some speed. I felt like there were some opportunities after, to still overtake him, but then I waited maybe a bit too long.“The bit towards the final corner, there was only really one path where you could ride in. I tried to overtake, didn't really go anywhere.”Del Grosso announced that he will ride 13 races this cyclo-cross season – all of the 12 World Cup rounds and the World Championships in Oostend.Last season the Dutchman came into his first elite season from the under-23 ranks and finished 14th in his opening race at the World Cup round at Namur in mid-December. Before racing in Ostrava, the 23-year-old joked that a 13th place finish Friday would be an improvement of last year's first race.“I think a lot of people think about my [cyclo-cross] races from last season,” said Del Grosso. “Last year I also needed some time to get into it. I didn’t prepare to be here in my best shape.” Del Grosso looked comfortable on the slippery terrain in Ostrava and was able to follow Nys before putting his rival under pressure in the final laps. “I have mixed feelings, I can be quite happy with my race today. The feeling was not yet where it was supposed to be. It was a really tactical race with how the course was. I think I played it relatively well, but then the final two minutes was not perfect," he reflected.“I don't think it was a bad performance. Technically, I think it's a good 'cross. Some points for improvement, but also not crazy. A lot better than last year.”Del Grosso competed on the road this season with Alpecin-Premier Tech and won the NXT Classic in April then adding 14th in Amstel Gold Race. The Dutchman took a two-month break following his last road race in the Flandrien Classic and National Coach Gerben de Knegt believed that it has allowed the youngster to ‘rest and train well’.He told : "His road season has been somewhat disappointing for various reasons. He rested well and trained well. In other years, he also started the [cyclo-cross] season quite quickly after his road campaign. “Now he is better prepared because he has been able to train for more weeks between the end of the road season and the start of his cyclo-cross winter.”The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. Plus, the Cyclingnews app means you can stay up-to-date wherever you go!

item.title: 100% wear in 15 laps - Qatar tyre issue has got even worse
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Despite the highest front tyre pressures of the season and a maximum stint length already in place, Pirelli is evaluating if further precautions are needed for the Qatar Grand Prix after Friday practice served up “surprise after surprise.”The Lusail circuit is already the most challenging of the season for tyres, but the evidence from the first day of track running has shown graining, wear and degradation to be at higher levels than anticipated pre-event.It is suspected this has been caused by a more weathered track surface and the reduced downforce levels of the 2026 cars that are causing sliding.On a weekend where there is a much-talked-about 27-lap maximum stint length laid down for each set of tyres, Pirelli has already seen evidence of the most abused front-left sets hitting 100% wear in localised areas after just 15 laps of running on Friday.Pirelli’s chief engineer Simone Berra said: “It's quite impressive the surprises that this circuit gives to us every time they come here.”Graining has been encountered on all three compounds - with it particularly aggressive on the C2 and C3. This is accelerating the wear in two specific areas of the tyre - near the inside shoulder and then on the very outside shoulder.And it is in these specific areas where early analysis has pointed to some wear indicators having hit the 100% level after just 15 laps of high-fuel running in practice.These elements are also contributing to Qatar producing levels of thermal decay degradation not seen in the past - up to 0.2 seconds per lap - which is going to have an impact on strategies as drivers will not be able to keep pushing on with stints as they have in the past.On top of all this, Pirelli has also found evidence of gravel cuts in rubber that was returned to it after Friday practice.Berra said: “We have seen some of them quite deep into the construction. There was also a red flag due to this, and it's something that obviously in a circuit like this, it's an additional variable that can create some attention from our side in terms of punctures.”Gravel stone cuts discovered after Friday practice last year prompted Pirelli to increase tyre pressures ahead of Saturday running - and a repeat response has not been ruled out right now.“We are evaluating all the variables,” he said. “If necessary, we will increase the pressure.”Front pressures are currently at the 29psi set before the weekend, which is the highest they have ever been heading into an event and at the same level Pirelli settled on from Saturday onwards in Qatar last year.If Pirelli chooses to raise the pressures any more, then they will be the highest they have been in the modern era of F1.However, Berra is well aware that raising pressures will likely serve to reduce the contact patch of the tyres even more which could potentially increase graining even more.“That's why I wouldn't increase the pressure if possible,” he said. “But if we have to for integrity reasons, obviously we are going to evaluate it.”The other action Pirelli is considering in response to the findings about extreme wear of the tyres is reducing the maximum stint length from its current 27 laps.Berra said that analysis would take place in Pirelli’s laboratory on the tyres used on Friday to see if there are any concerns about their integrity.“We are going to check them, to section them, and obviously if there is no integrity issue, we will keep the 27 laps in any case because we know that graining level will reduce for the race, and the teams will do much more management to extend the stint length.“It's an analysis that is ongoing in our laboratory and, with our usual prescription review, we are going to understand if we continue with 27 or not.”Even if the situation is a marginal one, reducing the stint length may not necessarily be needed because, with degradation in play, Pirelli’s analysis is that it would make no sense for teams to run the maximum distance anyway as it would be too slow.Instead, with the race distance being 57 laps it is much more logical for teams to split their stints in three equal ones of 19 laps.However, teams could be forced to shuffle things around based on the timing of safety cars. So even if they headed into the race not intending to run tyres to the maximum distance, they could be tempted to trying to eke out a final 27-lap stint if safety car timing fell that way.Berra thinks however that the degradation levels seen mean that pace-wise it would not make sense to run for 27 laps - and early safety cars would more likely turn the race into a three-stopper.

item.title: Blue Jays sign former Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr.
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: The moment that the Yankees decided to pass on giving free agent second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. the one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, his fate was all but set in stone. It was almost the exact same situation as a couple years ago with Gleyber Torres, who also had a perfectly reasonable case to at least be given the option of returning to New York on a one-year, make-good QO. But for one reason or another, the Yankees’ front office came to the conclusion that they were at the end of the rope with Gleyber, and the same has come to fruition with Jazz.Chisholm found a new home today and it’s still in the AL East: Toronto. The Blue Jays came to terms with the second baseman on a one-year, $18.5 million deal for 2027 ($12.5 million in salary plus a $6 million signing bonus) that also has a funky option for 2028. It’s a $16 million player option, but if Jazz declines it, then the Jays still have a chance to bring him back on a pretty big $40 million club option. If they decline that and give him a $1.5 million buyout, then he’s a free agent next offseason as well. So if Jazz has a great year for Toronto and thinks he could beat $16 million, then Toronto still has a chance to bring him back on a hefty price tag, albeit hefty for just one year. The bottom line is that he’s locked into $34.5 million even if he repeats his up-and-down 2026 or regresses. Chisholm’s 2026 campaign with the Yankees was a bit of a mess and we don’t need to go back into it in great detail. It was a disappointing walk year and we subsequently gave it a poor grade in our report card series. In a vaccum, Jazz was still productive in 2026 (a 98 wRC+ and good defense per FanGraphs still gave him 3.5 fWAR), but his slugging tumbled from a 30/30 guy in 2025 with .491 SLG to 19 homers with a .399 SLG. That looks bad when mixed in with his worst strikeout rates since 2023, and his highest in any season of at least 400 plate apperances. Still, Chisholm stole 41 bases as well and it’s not hard to envision a scenario where he becomes a pest again next year. It’s a reasonable gamble from Toronto’s perspective, and even if you’re tired with Jazz’s bit, the prospect of “Anthony Volpe, 2027 Yankees second baseman” isn’t particularly enthralling, either.The high-variance outcomes at the plate seem to have alarmed the Yankees, and they probably also weren’t entirely thrilled by other incidents surrounding him. Your mileage may vary on them, but I know that I was personally more annoyed by unapologetic postgame quote after a brutal postseason error than the lollipop incident, which was just goofy. Jazz is Jazz. The Blue Jays’ fans will find this to be true as well. Now, will he come closer to the superlative 2025 version or the chaotic 2026 version? We’ll learn the answer from a distance — but not too much of a distance. I’ve already made my guess.

item.title: Winners & losers from F1 2026 Qatar GP Friday practice
item.author: Scott Mitchell-Malm
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli led Mercedes team-mate George Russell in both Friday Formula 1 practice sessions for the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, including an FP2 that was punctuated by two red flags.Some drivers struggled more than others - and a few lost considerable running over the opening practice sessions - but who are the winners and losers from Friday in Qatar?Loser: Ferrari (7th & 8th)If you ask Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton pulling over to the side of the road with a power issue in FP2 was likely the least of Ferrari's worries!Hamilton was running an older engine for practice, so Leclerc seemed unperturbed by the issue. The bigger problem is that the "pace has just been very, very poor", reckons Leclerc."We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2 and it's very difficult to understand what is the outlier."It didn't help that time was wasted changing Leclerc's floor after a spin, but that just distracted from what is Ferrari's real issue. It's slow by any measure and has a big night to try and fix it. Pirelli’s rubber is taking a battering around the Qatar track - which has sealed its status as the most challenging of the season for tyres.The Lusail venue delivers graining, high wear, high carcass temperatures because of the fast corners and fatigue risks, plus extra jeopardy caused by gravel stones - and this year things are worse than predicted pre-event.A combination of the weathered track surface that has got rougher allied to 2026 downforce and performance levels have come together to produce high levels of localised graining that is resulting in some sets reaching 100% wear in localised areas after just 15 laps.Despite the highest tyre pressures of the season, and a 27-lap maximum stint length for each set having been laid down, Pirelli is conducting analysis tonight to see if even more action needs to be taken ahead of qualifying day to avoid any risk of trouble in the race. Winner: Mercedes (1st & 2nd)After two consecutive weekends without a podium finish since wrapping up both its world championships, Mercedes looks in a mega place to end that mini streak here. It could hardly have hoped for a better Friday. It looks very well balanced, strong in all corner types, and there's a massive one-lap advantage and in the long run too. Both drivers seem pretty happy with how the car feels, and all of its rivals are worried and feel that Mercedes is in a league of its own. So this is about as good as any weekend has looked for Mercedes in a long time. Loser: Red Bull (5th & 6th)Though Mercedes thinks Red Bull could emerge as its nearest rival come qualifying, right now this is miles off the standard that Red Bull and Max Verstappen have been setting in recent races. There was a distinct air of unhappiness from the Red Bull camp on Friday evening, with Verstappen bemoaning a car that feels disconnected, a heavy steering problem needing resolving overnight, and just generally Red Bull not looking nearly as sorted with its car balance.Technical director Pierre Wache is not optimistic that the gap can be closed significantly because it is so big. So this is looking like at the moment Red Bull suffering a chastening Friday that leaves it with lower hopes for the rest of the weekend than its recent mega form would have had it believing in coming into the weekend. Winner: Racing Bulls (9th & 10th)You might look at Racing Bulls' performance and think, hmm, leading the midfield as is pretty much usual, nothing to see here.Peel back the layers and there's quite a lot more going on here.Its biggest issue is straightline speed, but, as Liam Lawson puts it, that's all "stuff we can see and should be able to fix".He says the team made a set-up change to an extent that is rarely seen between practice sessions in F1, which team boss Alan Permane confirmed was about adding more rotation into the car with most teams struggling with understeer."We already had quite a good car in P1 and now we have an even faster car," reckons Lawson, and the team has a big gap to the next team that only ran the mediums (Audi was closest but on the hards) on long runs. Loser: Pierre Gasly (10th & 12th)Gasly’s spin and subsequent beaching cost him valuable time in FP2, the session most representative of qualifying conditions. The Frenchman said he “should have probably not gone for it” as the tyres were below temperature, he hit the kerbs, and then lost control of the car - damaging the car’s floor in the process.Furthermore he was “not fully pleased” with the set-up - and Alpine’s managing director Steve Nielsen said the balance is “nowhere near where it needs to be”.This was never likely to be a great Alpine track given high-speed performance is its biggest weakness but now Gasly is even more on the back foot heading into Saturday.Winner: Rafael Camara (15th & 17th)Camara’s trouble-free Friday will come as a relief to the rookie who endured a rocky start to F1 in his home race. In Qatar, Camara finished ahead of Haas team-mate Ollie Bearman but his long-run pace is of greater importance.The Brazilian was right on par with Bearman in FP2, under a tenth slower than the Briton over his stint. It’s looking like the most useful running yet in this cameo ahead of his full-season F1 debut. Loser: Aston Martin (19th & 20th)This is looking like a slightly better weekend for Aston Martin than in Las Vegas, but that comes with the extremely big asterisk that it couldn't really be worse. As it stands, better might just mean not fighting with Cadillac. There are no long runs to be able to judge the team on partly because of the biggest issue of the day, which is that the car didn't seem particularly robust around the challenges of such a parts-breaking circuit. Aston Martin opted to call it a day with all the disruptions in order to fix what it could, having had a lot of downtime between and during the sessions to try and repair damage. Mike Krack predicted an evening bonding bits of carbon back together with glue, Lance Stroll has a back problem, and this looks like a tricky start to a weekend that Aston Martin had, in relative terms, slightly higher hopes for. Loser: Williams (14th & 16th)Williams hovered around P15 on Friday and neither driver started on the front foot, as both Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon had offs in FP1.Sainz’s long run was faster than Albon’s on average, but the pair are well behind the rest of the midfield - our analysis putting Williams almost a second behind next-best team Audi and behind Haas.The Spaniard said he failed to “close” his laps. “There's always snaps, always understeer, there's always a balance that maybe doesn't suit the whole lap and it's difficult to close it.”That doesn’t bode well for qualifying.

item.title: Bad luck for Lucinda Brand with mechanical issues in snowy opening round of cyclo-cross World Cup in Ostrava
item.author: Ben Goddard
item.content:encoded: The picturesque venue was a step into the unknown, with the Czech Republic hosting its first-ever World Cup event. While the snow and Christmas lights made for a unique setting at the former coal mine venue, the frozen surface and deep ruts made for dangerous conditions. The evening race saw temperatures drop below freezing, and Brand was one of several casualties of the frozen ground.At the halfway point, Brand was fighting in the top 10 before she couldn't clip into her pedals, a problem that many riders suffered during the elite women's and elite men's race.For the Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions rider, though, she was left frustrated and shouting at her pit crew as they desperately tried to solve the issue from the pits.Brand then lost over a minute and couldn't regain the time in the difficult conditions, finishing 15th and 2:25 behind race winner Marie Schreiber (SD Worx–Protime).Brand was not the only rider to struggle with her equipment, as race winner Schreiber and third-placed finisher Manon Bakker were both forced to change bikes due to frozen pedals.Despite having technical issues of her own, Bakker was hoping for more snow as the cyclo-cross World Cup continues in Tabor on Sunday. “I made too many mistakes to really get into the win. I think everybody struggled with their pedals, I couldn’t clip in at all. I had a mechanical with my first bike and had to change, which is where I lost quite a lot of time," Bakker said.“I came back, but that was it. I'd rather hope for more snow (at Tabor on Sunday). I think I'm the only one who was really smiling at the weather.”It was Brand’s first outing in these snow conditions after missing previous World Cup rounds in Val di Sole. “We haven’t had too often the chance for it,” said Brand on the snow conditions before the opening World Cup round. “I missed the World Cups in Val di Sole. This is something different again as there is not as much snow everywhere [on the course itself].”Brand won the overall cyclo-cross World Cup series last year after sweeping the opening seven rounds in a commanding season.However, this season the Dutch woman has found racing much closer and was beaten on two occasions last weekend by Sara Casasola. In the second of those races, Brand fell heavily at the X2O 'cross in Beringen and commented about suffering rib pain afterwards."My rib hurts a little. I now have to breathe well and calmly," Brand said. “It needs to heal again. It remains to be seen how this will develop in the coming days. You can do nothing but wait and let it recover.”Brand won the World Cup overall by 97 points ahead of Aniek Van Alphen (777TV CX Team). However, with Van Alphen finishing runner-up in Ostrava, the pressure is on the two-time World Champion as they head to the second round in Tabor on Sunday.
