item.title: World Cup Ostrava: Thibau Nys surges ahead of Tibor Del Grosso to triumph in elite men's snowy first round
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Reigning European champion Thibau Nys (Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions) held off Dutch champion Tibor Del Grosso (Alpecin-Premier Tech) on the final corner and won the opening round of the UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup in Ostrava, Czech Republic.Michael Vanthourenhout (Pauwels Sauzen-Altez Industriebouw Cycling Team) then nabbed the final spot on the podium with a final push through blowing snow ahead of of Cameron Mason (777tv CX Team) in fourth and Jente Michels (Alpecin-Premier Tech) in fifth.Nys continued his string of victories, dominating the X2O Trofee series with a trio of wins this month and taking the ’cross continental title."It was a really difficult one, but I think it's in my top three of most beautiful cyclo-cross victories. I think the fans, the atmosphere, the chorus, the snow makes it one to remember," Nys told broadcasters at the finish.Nys let out a loud scream as he crossed the line, only able to drop Del Grosso in the final 200 metres with a more powerful sprint. Nys admitted he overcame two slow leaks and pitted for a fresh bike twice, then used "good technique" to seal the victory."I had two flat tyres, so it kept pushing me a little bit back. I didn't lose a lot because it [tyre pressure] was slowly going out, but it kept pushing me a bit out of the race. And then when I found my way to the front, I tried to make a move and push hard. Then on the last lap, I managed it perfectly and did a good sprint," he noted."I was feeling way, way better than the last two weekends, just physically. But then of course you come here on a circuit where it's difficult to release the full power, so the fact that I can finish it off like this is a proof that my cyclo-cross skills are still there."The World Cup season opened with two rounds in Czechia, the elite fields competing Friday in Ostrava in the only night races of the 12-round series. Floodlights illuminated a blanket of snow covering the venue, with the temperature holding steady for most of the afternoon at -1°C, but the wind chill making it feel five degrees colder.Niels Vandeputte (Alpecin-Premier Tech Development) put on the power beside Nys from the start and took the front spot on the twisty course. Vanthourenhout and Del Grosso then led the long line of riders through the first pass of the finish line, riding in 6:36, which was the slowest lap of the nine.There were narrow ruts instead of mud from the elite women’s race as the temperatures remained below freezing, and holiday lights sprinkled around the circuit. Amid the sounds of cowbells and cheers, the ringing of disc brakes was heard with constant speed changes as the track was slippery.On the start of lap three, Gerben Kuypers (Pauwels Sauzen-Altez Industriebouw) took the lead ahead of Del Grosso and Pauwels teammate Vanthourenhout as small gaps began to form in the field of 75 riders.At the mid-point of the contest, 10 riders settled in at the front - Del Grosso between the Pauwels Sauzen duo of Kuypers and Nieuwenhuis, then Vanthourenhout, Nys, Kuypers, Jent Michels, Yordi Corsus, Witse Meeussen, Felipe Orts and Cameron Mason.It was Nys who drove the pace at the front to start the sixth and seventh laps, the second time carving a gap of five seconds to chasers across the stairs. However, he had to slow to bang one foot on the pedal to clear debris from his cleat and it was game-on again. Dutch ’cross champion Del Grosso, Vanthourenhout, Kuypers, Michels and Mason made it to his back wheel, but others were distanced for good.On the final lap, Del Grosso took command at the front with Nys glued to his wheel, Vanthourenhout third and Mason in fourth. In a corner, Vanthourenhout dove to the front of the lead trio and held the position into the tricky descent from the stairs, while Nys made a pass of Del Grosso to nab second position.With the wind blowing light snow, Del Grosso and Nys went back into the front positions, Vanthourenhout losing momentum in a corner before the barriers. Nys made the pass before the short steps feature and drove the sprint to the line and keep his winning streak alive.Thibau Nys (Bel) Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau LionsTibor Del Grosso (Ned) Alpecin-Premier TechMichael Vanthourenhout (Bel) Pauwels Sauzen-Altez IndustriebouwCameron Mason (Gbr) 777TV CX TeamJente Michels (Bel) Alpecin-Premier TechWitse Meeussen (Bel) Crelan-CorendonGerben Kuypers (Bel) Pauwels Sauzen-Altez IndustriebouwKevin Kuhn (Sui) Heizomat-CubeYordi Corsus (Bel) Pauwels Sauzen-Altez IndustriebouwJoran Wyseure (Bel) Crelan-CorendonMees Hendrikx (Ned) Team Bomba JOINJoris Nieuwenhuis (Ned) Heizomat-CubeGuus van den Eijnden (Ned) 777TV CX TeamNiels Vandeputte (Bel) Alpecin-Premier TechMartin Groslambert (Fra) Sebmotobikes CX TeamDanny van Lierop (Ned) Heizomat-CubeLaurens Sweeck (Bel) Crelan-CorendonArthur van den Boer (Bel) Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau LionsRyan Kamp (Ned) Team Bomba JOINVictor Van de Putte (Bel) Charles Liégeois CX TeamStefano Viezzi (Ita) Alpecin-Premier TechDavid Haverdings (Ned) Alpecin-Premier TechFlorian Fery (Fra) Team CX TPMJarno Bellens (Bel) Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions

item.title: 'Bring great bike racing to the people' - Two events debut at USA CRITS for seven races compressed across 22 days in 2027
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: The Tour of Newport News Criterium and Charlotte Criterium make debuts in the USA CRITS series in 2027, with the compact collection of seven one-day races now spanning 22 days for overall elite rider and team titles, condensing the calendar by a full month.In its 18th season, with races clustered in four states of the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast regions, the series opener will take place in Newport News, Virginia, on April 10. The finale is set for the High Line Criterium in Suwanee, Georgia, on May 1.Noticeably absent from the calendar is the Sunny King Criterium, which had been the lead-off event the past three seasons. Anniston has hosted races for state age-group championships as well as collegiate conference championships and organisers will continue to hold two days of racing for a 25th edition April 10-11.“Nearly 20 years after launching the series, we're still bringing the best riders in the country to communities that embrace the excitement of professional cycling," Gene Dixon, founder of Athens Twilight Criterium and owner of Swagger LLC that produces USA CRITS, said in a press release."When we started Athens Twilight in 1980, the idea was simple: bring great bike racing to the people. USA CRITS was built on that same philosophy."Dixon told that the compact calendar helped simplify travel for riders and teams, especially those traveling from outside the US. While the final set of three races continue to conflict for some teams with Tour of the Gila, April 28-May 2, the earlier finish for the criterium series opens travel for all teams to compete at Tour de Bloom, May 12-16. Also a postivite is that the USA CRITS calendar does not bump into rushed travel to Washington, D.C. for the Amazon Armed Forces Cycling Classic, now early June.All USA CRITS races will provide live streaming, produced by Swagger. Last year's prize purse totalled $200,000, with equal payouts for elite men and women across individual races and overall series classifications. The USA CRITS D1 Team programme also returns in 2027, with eligible teams provided travel stipends.The Tour of Newport News is a three-day, five-race event that takes place on the Virginia Peninsula, on the banks of the Hampton Roads harbor near the Atlantic Ocean. USA Cycling-sanctioned events that comprise the omnium include a points race at Todd Stadium, a hill climb up an eight-story parking garage, a time trial and two criteriums. Only the Newport News Twilight Criterium, under the street lights on Saturday night, will set the standings for USA CRITS on Saturday, April 10.The Charlotte Criterium is a new race that takes place on Friday, April 23, the night before the Winston Salem Cycling Classic. Specifics about the location of the course and start times will be confirmed in the coming months.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Garmin's brilliant Varia rearview radar is usually pricey, but you can now grab the RTL515 for less than $150 in this Black Friday deal
item.author: Paul Norman
item.content:encoded: A rearview radar has become a must-have accessory for many road cyclists, alerting them to approaching vehicles, how close they are and how fast they're going. One of the best available is the Garmin RLT515, and this Black Friday it's got 25% off at Backcountry, dropping the price from $200 to just $149.99 for US buyers.In the UK, Sigma Sports has the RTL515 discounted to £117, down from £169.99; that's a hefty 31% saving.The market for rearview radars is now quite crowded, but it was Garmin that introduced the category with its first-generation Varia, and it's still arguably the leading brand. The RTL515 has a claimed detection distance of 140m, although on a straight road in good conditions we reckon it's significantly greater than this. The 220-degree detection angle ensures that vehicles approaching from side roads are detected as well.The radar links up to a cycling computer, a smartwatch or a phone via Bluetooth or ANT+ and alerts you when a vehicle is detected. It's device-agnostic, so it will work with any brand of cycling computer, not just Garmin.A fast-approaching vehicle generates a different alert from a slower-moving one, and cycling computers and other devices display how close it is. Once it's passed, there's an all-clear alert.Four lighting modes include a day flash with 16 hours of claimed battery runtime, a night flash, a constant mode and Peloton mode that lowers the output so that other riders behind you in a group aren't dazzled.The RTL515 is low in weight at a claimed 71g and is supplied with a robust mount, O-rings to secure it to your seatpost and spacers to suit different seatpost shapes.REI has a similar 25% Black Friday discount on the Garmin Varia RCT715, which includes a camera in addition to the tail light and is priced down from $400 to $299.99, while the newer Varia RearVue 820 is priced down from $300 to $249.99.

item.title: Mini-pumps begone! The Cycplus AS2 electric inflator is a third off this Black Friday, making it cheaper than many hand pumps
item.author: Paul Norman
item.content:encoded: Are the days of the mini pump over? The Cycplus AS2 electric pump is priced down to just $47.49 in the US and £38.95 in the UK on Amazon this Black Friday. It's the lowest price we've seen for this tiny electric pump and a third off the full retail price that you'd have paid last summer, making it cheaper than many of its competitors and many mini pumps too.With a claimed weight of just 87g (3oz), it's lighter than most mini pumps. It's smaller too and pocketable, measuring 65 x 44 x 28mm (2.6 x 1.7 x 1.1 inches). It's supplied with a hose, which you can use to reduce the risk of melting the valve on a TPU inner tube, although it can be directly hooked up to your valve if you're running tubeless or have a less delicate tube to inflate. We've spent too many hours standing by the road pumping up tubes not to be impressed by the Cycplus pump's around a minute to inflate a tyre to 50psi and it should manage two tyres on a charge. It's had a battery upgrade since launch too, upping the capacity from 300mAh to 400mAh, which Cycplus reckons will get two 25mm tyres to 110psi, if you like a firm ride. An LED indicator changes from green to amber to red as charge drops. Plug it into a USB-C charger and it will recharge in a claimed time of just 25 minutes. It comes with the necessary USB-C cable, a range of adapters and a silicone protective sleeve, plus a water resistant ziplock pouch. If you want to check that your tyre is really up to 110psi before setting off, the Cycplus AS2 Pro has a digital pressure gauge built in. It's a little larger and heavier, but will still fit in a jersey pocket with space to space.

item.title: World Cup Ostrava: Marie Schreiber cruises to first round elite women's victory on snow-packed course in Czech Republic
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: After the disappointment of being relegated at the European Championships, Marie Schreiber (SD Worx-Protime) bounced back with a triumph at the first UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup of the season in Ostrava, Czech Republic.The Luxembourg rider took a solo win in snowy conditions, ahead of runner-up Aniek van Alphen (777 CX Team) and third-placed Manon Bakker. Zoe Bäckstedt (Canyon-SRAM) took fourth, while Ceylin del Carmen Alvarado (Fenix-Premier Tech) was forced to settle for fifth after a crash with two laps to go.After a slow start and what appeared to be pedal issues, world champion Lucinda Brand (Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureu Lions) finished 15th at 2:25 behind the day’s winner and new World Cup leader, Schreiber.“This was special. It was really nice and something completely new. Yeah, I’ve done one snowy race before but it was a new course, an evening race, it was snowy and cold, and the crowds were amazing, so it was really special. It was awesome,” Schreiber said in a post-race interview to broadcasters.“At the first part, I had some problems with me pedals, like everyone did, it was really hard to clip in, but then I changed bikes and it was better. Like last week, I needed 20 minutes to get into the race ... but I just settled into a rhythm and try not to make mistakes. "I couldn’t go all out but had to go with the flow and be really smooth. I managed well, and once I caught Aniek, I could see on some parts I was stronger, I played it smart on the last lap and luckily it worked out.”The cyclo-cross stars lined up for the opening round of the UCI World Cup under snowy conditions, facing deep ruts along the circuit in Ostrava.Although Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) was missing from the start, the field was stacked with the likes of world champion Brand, Sara Casasola (Crelan-Corendon) and Fem van Empel (Specialized TMRW), all among the favourites for the night-time cyclo-cross race.Also on the start line was Shirin van Anrooij, who will have to start the races in a neutral kit for the first five weeks of the cyclo-cross season under UCI regulations, until January 1, when she can wear the kit of her new team, Canyon-SRAM.A slow start for Brand and Casasola saw the pair racing much further back on the opening circuit than expected, as van Alphen immediately took the lead.After the first lap, Van Alphen was followed by Alvarado and Schreiber in her wake. She continued her dominance, distancing her rivals and holding an eight-second advantage on the fourth of seven laps ahead of a chasing Schreiber and Bakker. Further back, Alvarado was 22 seconds back, and Kristýna Zemanova (Crelan-Corendon) was 42 seconds.Although Brand appeared to be gaining time back, moving up to sixth place about 25 seconds back, bad luck struck, and she was forced into the pits for a bike change after a problem with her pedals. She lost significant time, chasing in 22nd place at 1:34 behind the leader.Bad luck for Alvarado, too, who crashed on the fifth of seven laps, over the handlebars, through the deep snowy ruts, but was up and back on her bike quickly, chasing in fourth place, but with Backstedt close behind.Under two laps to go, Van Alphen still held a small lead, but with only one second ahead of Schreiber, the pair reconnected as they hit the snow circuit, resetting the race for the victory. The race became even more interesting as Bakker caught the leading duo after a new fastest lap of 7:04, showing strong late-race form.Schreiber made the winning move on the last lap, opening a small gap to Bakker and Van Alphen, who appeared to struggle to clip in to her pedals.They were no match for Schreiber, who crossed the line for the win, with Van Alphen taking second and Bakker third, not only winning the first round but also taking the series lead.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Antonelli tops Qatar FP2 after multiple red flag delays
item.author: Samarth Kanal
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli led Mercedes team-mate George Russell again on Friday as two red flags flew in an extended Formula 1 FP2 session in Qatar.Antonelli set the benchmark of 1m23.077s on medium tyres before a red flag was flown midway through FP2 for gravel and debris from an early spin for Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc.Shortly after the session resumed, Alpine’s Pierre Gasly beached his car in the gravel to bring out the second red flag. Late on in FP2, the session was extended by 13 minutes.Russell was 0.127s off his team-mate with neither Mercedes driver improving on soft tyres as they were both interrupted by stoppages. Antonelli had however set the fastest first sector on softs before the second red flags flew.McLaren pair Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri were third and fourth respectively, and around 0.45s off the leading Mercedes. They lined up ahead of Red Bull duo Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar who were half a second off Antonelli’s leading pace.Half a second behind Hadjar was Leclerc in seventh, with his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton in eighth. Hamilton cut across Verstappen late in the session but the stewards deemed no further investigation was necessary.The seven-time champion stopped off track with four minutes remaining, triggering a virtual safety car, as his Ferrari lost power.Racing Bulls completed the top 10 with Liam Lawson ninth and 0.1s ahead of team-mate Arvid Lindblad.Alpine’s Gasly - whose progress was halted by that trip into the gravel - finished between the Audis of Gabriel Bortoleto in 11th and Nico Hulkenberg in 13th.Williams' Alex Albon was 14th and team-mate Carlos Sainz was 16th, as they were split by Franco Colapinto in the second Alpine.Rafael Camara was 17th and ahead of Ollie Bearman as Haas eclipsed the Aston Martins and Cadillac rounded out the standings.

item.title: The Guardian view on AI and the Riemann hypothesis: a triumph of intelligence, a test of democracy | Editorial
item.author: Editorial
item.content:encoded: Machines are solving problems that have been beyond the reach of human ingenuity. Their growing power must not become the sole preserve of billionairesFor the average person, the news that AI has helped crack a problem that has defied mathematicians since 1859 might elicit momentary awe. What ought to worry everyone is not the discovery per se, but what it says about the power of the machines making it. The pace of scientific discovery looks like it is outrunning the ability of humanity – and its institutions – to understand, let alone regulate, AI’s advances.Last Friday Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, said that he, with the assistance of an unreleased version of the company’s Claude chatbot, had produced what many mathematicians see as the holy grail: a proof for the Riemann hypothesis. Mathematicians like Cornell University’s Steven Strogatz had already cried on podcasts, lamenting that students were asking: “What’s the point if the AI can do math better than any human being?” Computers can validate the Alpöge-Claude proof. But Prof Strogatz fears AI’s discoveries may soon defy human understanding. Asking AI to explain them, he said, would be like him trying to teach calculus to his own dog.Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? item.title: Percy Jackson, the Helm of Hades, and Annabeth Chase’s Yankees hat
item.author: John Griffin
item.content:encoded: Earlier today, the third and fourth episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians season three premiered on Disney+. Adapted from the Rick Riordan books of the same name, the series centers on the titular son of Poseidon as he and his friends grappled with the gods and monsters of the ancient Greeks and Romans, alive and well and living in North America. Two years ago, in the aftermath of the season one finale (and our Top 100 Yankees series here at Pinstripe Alley), I dove into Yankees history, asking the rather amusing question, “Which legendary Yankees figures were secretly the gods of Mt. Olympus?”As the new season of the television show approached, I found myself thinking about another place where Percy Jackson and baseball intersect: Annabeth Chase’s Yankees hat. A gift from her mother, the goddess Athena, the Yankees hat is more than a simple baseball cap, also functioning as a magical item that turns the wearer invisible. For those who know Greek mythology, it is a clear reference to the Helm of Hades (also known variously as the Helm of Darkness, the Cap of Hades, and the Cap of Invisibility), a magical item normally associated with the God of the Underworld but which others use sporadically throughout Greek mythological history.Within the Percy Jackson universe, items and places from Greek myths are reimagined all the time: Mt. Olympus is in the Empire State Building, Charon the ferryman is an elevator operator, and Apollo’s sun chariot is a sports car. And so I began to wonder, why did the author decide to make a magical item inspired by the Helm (but which is itself not the helm — that specific item appears elsewhere in the story) out of a Yankees hat?To answer that question, we first need to dive a bit into the mythical helm. While it’s hard to find an ancient depiction of it, here’s how Renaissance and Enlightenment era artists tended to depict it, as seen through this statue of Perseus holding the head of Medusa:Sure, this doesn’t help us understand what the ancient one looked like (that’s a bit harder to determine), but it does show us that… well, it’s not some big special thing, just a normal everyday item that is imbued with magical properties. This, in fact, reflects most things in mythology: modern depictions of Cerberus, the guard dog of Hades, depict him as a big, scary monster, but in antiquity he was just a simple dog that happened to have three heads; see, for example, this statue group of Hades, Persephone, and Cerberus from the first century BCE:With that in mind, it’s clear that, for a modern day invisibility cap, Riordan was looking not for something extraordinary and noticeable, but rather something incredibly mundane. And in the United States in the 21st century, what headwear is more mundane than a baseball cap? I mean, baseball caps with the logos of basketball, football, hockey, and soccer teams are everywhere. Colleges and high schools plaster their school logo on them. Even the US military and veterans’ organizations employ baseball caps, both as part of certain uniforms and as non-uniform gear. The baseball cap has spread well beyond its original use on the diamond, and has become one of, if not arguably the, American fashion accessory.So it makes sense why Riordan would make the modern-day cap of invisibility out of a baseball cap. But why, specifically, a Yankees hat? It could simply be narrative convenience — the Percy Jackson series centers on New York, and when people think of baseball hats in New York City, they tend to think of Yankee hats (apologies to any Mets fans reading this, but it’s true). Narrative convenience, though, is not in my mind a sufficient answer, even if it hints at the real answer: the author immediately jumps from baseball cap to Yankee hat because, ultimately, the Yankee hat is the default baseball cap not just in New York, but within public consciousness. Check out, for example, the Wikipedia page for “baseball cap;” at the time of writing, the top image on the page, normally designed to give the reader an understanding of the topic, is a Yankee hat. And so, when trying to create the most mundane, unexciting, run-of-the-mill modern hat? Well, in truth, there’s only one option.

item.title: 'The Kärcher OC3 pressure washer is so useful that I can’t imagine life without it' – It's got 28% off in the Black Friday Amazon deal
item.author: paul.brett@futurenet.com (Paul Brett)
item.content:encoded: If you’ve ever loaded a mud-caked bike into the back of a clean car because there wasn't a hose in sight, this Black Friday cycling deal is worth a serious look. Amazon has cut 28% off the Kärcher OC3, dropping this ultra-handy portable washer from £119.99 down to a record-low £86.99, which beats the previous best of £92.99.Unlike heavy-duty mains pressure washers, which require power, a tap, and enough restraint not to blast grease out of your bottom bracket or strip paintwork, the battery-operated OC3 delivers gentle, bike-safe pressure anywhere you want. Elsewhere, the Kärcher OC 3 Foldable, which I awarded an almost perfect 4.5-star rating, is also discounted to £98.99, 29% off the usual £139.99. The OC3 Foldable, of course, the clue is in the name, folds down to a super compact size, but still has a larger capacity of 8 litres, over the 4 litres of the standard OC3.Both models produce the same low-pressure output of 5 bar (72 psi), which is more than enough for bike-related cleaning, and battery run time is also around 15 mins on both too.The original OC3 is cheaper, but the OC3 Foldable is the newer model, and it has a few key upgrades that, in my opinion, make it better. It has a larger capacity tank and USB-C charging, meaning you can charge it off a power bank or car charger.The Kärcher OC3 Pressure Washer earned a glowing review, and right now it undercuts the newer OC3 Foldable on price. While the updated model brings a few extra conveniences to the table, core performance between the two remains very close, making the standard OC3 the clear winner if value for money is your priority.I love the Kärcher OC3 Foldable Pressure Washer, its suberbly portable, has a larger tank and better charging functionality than its older sibling. You can also draw water from anywhere without additional accessories (the original needs this). It costs more than its sibling, but with £41 off, if you want the additional features, I think it's a price worth paying.These Kärcher deals apply to UK shoppers only, and I've not found any significant deals on either of the OC3 models at Amazon US, with only 7% off the OC3.The Muc-Off Mobile Pressure Washer Starter bundle is also a recommended bike-friendly cleaner (although it's not particularly mobile); it's still a great option. The Starter Bundle is discounted to £187.50, 25% off the usual £250 at Muc-Off in a limited-time deal.Below are the best Kärcher deals from other retailers, relevant to your location and currency.

item.title: Netcompany Ineos cancel new transfer Harold Tejada before 2027 season amid biological passport anti-doping investigation
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Netcompany Ineos have agreed to terminate the agreement with one of their new signings for the 2027 season before his contract even begins on January 1, amid a provisional suspension and investigation into the biological passport of Colombian rider Harold Tejada. Not even 50 days have passed since Ineos announced Tejada as a new name set to bolster their climbing ranks, but after he revealed on Friday afternoon that he had been notified by the International Testing Agency (ITA) of an anti-doping disciplinary proceeding against him, an announcement from the British team followed an hour later. "Netcompany INEOS and Harold Tejada have agreed to end their agreement for the 2027 season, before he was due to join the team on 1 January," read a post from the team on X. A winner of a Paris-Nice stage this season, Tejada was set to be one of nine new transfers already announced for Netcompany Ineos in 2027, as they look to rebuild back to their former GC glory. Tejada maintains his innocence. His statement highlighted that the suspension is "a temporary measure, which does not constitute a sanction nor a definitive decision", and he confirmed that he will be working with a legal and medical team to "exercise my defense before the relevant bodies, through the established channels."The ITA released a press release, echoing Tejada's statement, but also confirming that it had charged Tejada with an anti-doping rule violation (ADRV) "for the use of a prohibited substance or a prohibited method based on unexplained abnormalities in his athlete biological passport (ABP).""The ITA reports that the ABP¹ of Colombian road cyclist Harold Alfonso Tejada Canacue has returned an Adverse Passport Finding (APF)² due to unexplained abnormalities in the values of his haematological ABP," read the release. "Specifically, a panel of experts has confirmed that the rider has a case to answer, as, after reviewing the rider’s explanation, the panel maintained that the abnormalities in his ABP are highly likely to have been caused by the administration of a prohibited substance and/or a prohibited method."The rider has been informed of the charge and has the right to provide additional information. The rider has the possibility to accept the consequences for his violation or to request for the matter to be referred to the UCI Anti-Doping Tribunal for a hearing."Further, in accordance with the UCI anti-doping rules and article 6.2.1 of the UCI regulations for results management (UCI RMR), a mandatory provisional suspension has been imposed on the rider. The rider has the right to challenge the provisional suspension and ask for its lifting."As listed on the ITA's website: "The ABP is an individual electronic profile that monitors selected biological variables of an athlete. It contains the results of the athletes’ urine and blood samples, which are tracked consistently. Any significant variation from normal levels can be assessed for possible manipulation. At the ITA, ABP management is performed by a specialist unit of experts who liaise with the Athlete Passport Management Units (APMUs) and ABP Expert Panels in order to issue further targeted testing or in case of adverse or atypical findings."Tejada's statement in full"To the general public, cycling fans, and everyone who has accompanied me throughout my career: on November 26, 2026, I was notified by the International Testing Agency (ITA), on behalf of the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI), of the initiation of an anti-doping disciplinary proceeding against me."While this proceeding is being resolved, I am provisionally suspended in relation to an investigation into my biological passport."I want to clarify that this suspension is a temporary measure, which does not constitute a sanction or a final decision."From day one, I have acted with diligence and responsibility, providing all requested information in a timely manner. I will continue to do so throughout the entire process, with full respect for the anti-doping authorities and cycling institutions."My legal and medical team will work to exercise my defense before the relevant bodies, through the established channels."In consideration of the confidentiality of the proceeding, I will refrain from making additional statements while the case is ongoing."I deeply thank my family, my friends, and all the people who have expressed their support to me during these days. I ask you, with all due respect, to understand this moment and respect our privacy."Harold Alfonso Tejada Canacue"The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: The best Black Friday deals Ars could find
item.author: Lee Hutchinson
item.content:encoded: Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005.It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City—heroes, all of them!—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator, against which there appeared to be no defense.And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: "Megatron must be stopped, ." The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday.

item.title: How the Knicks can advance in the NBA Cup
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: After the Knicks’ valiant comeback effort at Gainbridge Fieldhouse came up empty on November 13, they fell to 6-6 on the season and 0-2 in NBA Cup play. After an incredible run the year prior to claim the organization’s first trophy of any kind in 27 years (foreshadowing), they seemed fated to become the third consecutive NBA Cup champion to be bounced in the group stage.Yet, one six-game winning streak and an incredible fourth quarter in a Cup game against the Cavs later, and the Knicks are mathematically alive heading into Black Friday against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the red-hot Miami Heat.Now, after winning the Treble last year, experiencing the fatigue from last year’s Cup run that led to the 2-9 stretch from hell, and, you know, defending a real championship, a tournament that already had limited interest from Knicks fans seems to have the opposite intended effect, to the point where it might be beneficial to the knockout round altogether.But the Knicks are currently the only team to have never been grouped in Cup play, and since these games count toward the team’s 82-game record, there’s plenty to play for as the Knicks look to defend the first of their three trophies.Here’s a look at the current standings in East Group B and the East’s wild card, both of which are still in play:The simplest path is to win the group, which simply requires two things: to the Heat by in regulationWhat helps the Knicks here is their point differential. They lost the games to Philly and Indiana by five and two points respectively, which allowed their 19-point win over Cleveland to put them in a decent spot.Winning an NBA game by seven is the easy part; relying on an injured and struggling Pacers team to defeat the No. 1 seed in the East is another. Now, the Sixers look like a paper tiger with their clutch reliance (their Cup PD is negative because of this), but this reads like a game that would be a blowout.The current injury report has Jaylen Brown out with hamstring management and Joel Embiid questionable with an illness for the Sixers, while Tyrese Haliburton, Ben Sheppard, and Johnny Furphy are still out for Indiana. TJ McConnell, Larry Nance Jr., and Kelly Oubre Jr. are questionable.If the Sixers win, they clinch Group B. If they lose, the Knicks will get a shot at being the first 2-loss NBA Cup group winner in an unlikely five-way tie.In the event of a Sixers win, things get a lot more complicated.First of all, the Knicks would need there to be zero 3-1 non-group winners for obvious reasons. That means they’ll need losses from the Hawks, Pistons, and Raptors. Toronto already has a lower point differential, so margin wouldn’t matter there.Margin would matter with the other two. The Hawks are at +21 and the Pistons are at +31, so the Knicks are going to need to win and win by a lot to guarantee they get in.The simplest path to a wild card berth in the event of a Sixers win looks like this: Heat by The margin of victory would likely not need to be that big, as the more the Pistons and Hawks lose by, the more it knocks that down. The absolute minimum the Knicks would have to win by is seven to pass the Heat in point differential, but to only have to win by that much, they’d need the Bucks to win by 13 and the Celtics to win by 3.Which brings the difficulty aspect. You’re asking two of the worst teams in the league to win games against significantly better teams, one of which is a matchup between a 2-win Bucks team and the reigning No. 1 seed. That’s probably not happening.Also, there is the spoiler aspect that could theoretically damage both of these scenarios. If the Pacers (-27 PD) or Nets (-11 PD) win by such ridiculous margins, they would have a chance to steal a spot in the knockout round.Now, personally, a Hali-less Pacers team winning by damn near 50 or the Nets beating the Raptors by 30+ would be pretty stunning, but we’re already asking for stunning things to happen to get this far.In layman’s terms, a fourth consecutive trip to the knockout round is still unlikely, but possible.It’ll make for a fun night of scoreboard watching, that’s for sure.

item.title: 50-year-old structure led Williams to F1 cost cap breach
item.author: Josh Suttill
item.content:encoded: Williams has explained that overdue company restructuring triggered its Formula 1 cost cap penalty, as it made changes it thought were excluded from the cost cap. The team was found to have breached the 2025 cost cap by £627,000 (0.48% of the total cap) and will have to pay the FIA a financial penalty - as well as lose 1.5% of its windtunnel and CFD testing time for the next 12 months. Team boss James Vowles faced a number of questions on the breach during the Friday press conference in Qatar. “The background to it is that the company structure of Williams was largely unchanged from 1977 and wasn't really fit for purpose in a modern world,” Vowles said.“We went into it with every intention of being open, transparent with the FIA, which is what we held all the way throughout, but believed those costs, because it's company restructuring, [would] not be a cost cap expense.“It was the company restructuring that put us over. We’ve had no financial benefit from it, no sporting benefit as a result of it, and you can see that the penalty is pretty much adjusted to be in line with that as well at the same time.“But it was our interpretation of that, is that those costs are out of cap. The FIA’s interpretation of it are that they are in cap, and obviously we went with the FIA’s interpretation after much discussion.” Vowles called it a “one-off company restructuring” because the previous structure “wasn't quite fit for purpose”. Vowles encouraged “those interested” to look at Williams’s accounts on Companies House. According to Companies House, during 2025 the team “transferred much of its trade and assets to a newly formed subsidiary, Williams Grand Prix Engineering Services LLP, an entity in which the company is a 99% member. “This update to the corporate structure makes the organisation fit for the future, having been relatively unchanged in the nearly 50 years of operation since formation, “The changes are about future-proofing our business, enabling smarter ways of working and positioning us to stay competitive at the highest level. “The inclusion of a partner group will aid retention of certain staff and recognises the importance of those people to the delivery of the business plan. “Member distributions have been declared to the 1% member of Williams Grand Prix Engineering Services LLP.” Vowles described it as “Fundamentally, it's a single vertical structure as what was there previously. “There's many downsides to fundamentally having that. You'll see there's a number of other companies have been created around it, which is just more efficient.“The costs involved in it are fairly significant. If you think about what you have to do as a business, you probably have, in our case, close to 2,000 contracts with various suppliers and otherwise, that you have to migrate from one company to the next as a result of it. It's a very painful, lengthy task.“There's some legal that goes with it. There's some compliance you have to do in UK law as a result of it as well at the same time. “It was a process in the end that took, we initiated it probably around about six months, which probably gives you an idea as to how lengthy it is.“But it was using finance and legal personnel for that period of which we had to bolster up to get us through that period.” Williams fell down because it had a different interpretation of the regulations to the FIA.“Clearly, we should have done something differently as a result of it,” Vowles admitted. “Although the regulations aren't clear and black and white, it's interpretation, but the FIA is very clear on their perspective, which is the following: Because you've moved contracts from one business to the next, that effectively for them is procurement, which is an included activity. “For us, we defined it as a financial and legal activity because it's literally taking a contract and changing a name on it. “I can understand their interpretation, which is why we've accepted the breach, but I hope that helps you understand why it's subtleties, not clarity, really, in that circumstance.” Vowles isn’t too worried about that 1.5% reduction in windtunnel and CFD testing time given that under the Aerodynamic Testing Restrictions system, there’s a sliding scale of windtunnel and CFD time in 5% increments. “I think to put things in perspective, one position on the grid is 5% of ATR, and we've got a 1.5% delta. So it's less than a third of a position,” Vowles said.“I'm rather hoping that we do a better job next year and put ourselves back up the grid, and that would be 15% something in that ballpark. “So the reality is it's going to be small beans in the grand scheme of things.” Williams is currently ninth out of 11 teams as of the last ATR period, and that’s unlikely to change for the start of 2027. That table will then reset after the first ATR period ends halfway through 2027 - when by Vowles’s 15% ballpark estimation, Williams will hope to be around sixth in the championship.

item.title: It's only just been launched and Castelli's flagship jacket is already 25% off for Black Friday
item.author: Emily Tillett
item.content:encoded: The Castelli Perfetto is a familiar name in winter cycling. Alongside the iconic Gabba, it has been a go-to piece of kit for riders for more than a decade.When Castelli updated its Perfetto jacket in September, it took customer feedback on board. Riders had told the brand they wanted more warmth than the previous version offered - something our Associate Editor Josh Croxton also highlighted in his review of the Perfetto RoS 3. The new Perfetto 4 aims to address that feedback, with added warmth for cooler rides.Despite only launching around two months ago, the latest Perfetto is already discounted, with deals available across a range of sizes and colourways, and in both the men's and women's ranges. Designed for 'all-condition performance', it aims to offer a versatile layer that can handle a wide range of winter riding conditions, making it a useful addition to any cycling wardrobe - and now, it's available for less.UK readers can also save 20% on the latest Perfetto 4, bringing the price down to £224. The updated design addresses previous feedback around warmth, making it a more appealing option for colder rides.View DealThe jacket retains Castelli's highly breathable, windproof and water-repellent AirCore fabric, but it's now heavier. This change brings a slightly colder recommended temperature range of 4-12°C (39-53°F), compared to 4-14°C (39-57°F) for the previous Perfetto RoS 3.At the rear, the Perfetto 4 has a redesigned splash tail, while there are still three pockets, the outer two with a small drainage hole to prevent whatever you're carrying from being given their own private swimming pool.As for fit, Castelli describes the Perfetto 4 as having a race-inspired cut. Previous versions have impressed us with their fit, offering a close fit without being overly restrictive, while still leaving enough room underneath for an extra layer if needed. This is a premium winter cycling jacket, but the latest model is already enjoying significant discounts this Black Friday. If you're considering alternatives to the Perfetto 4, other winter jackets from Castelli currently discounted include the which is the Italian brand’s most wintery and most expensive outer layer. item.title: Mark Cavendish’s former coach joins Ben Swift among the staff reinforcements at Netcompany Ineos
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: British WorldTour team Netcompany Ineos have announced three new additions to their support staff, with the recently-retired Ben Swift, Vasilis Anastopoulos and Professor Asker Jeukendrup joining in the team’s backroom.As expected, after a 19-year career as a rider which included 15 race victories and two podium finishes in Milan-Sanremo, Swift will take up a role as one of the team’s sports directors. Having switched from a sprinter and Classics rider to a role as a road captain in recent years, he should be able to develop those leadership skills in his new role. "I know how much the people around a rider matter, because I've been that rider," Swift said in a team press release. "I'll miss racing, no doubt. But I'm excited to give something back from the car, keep learning, and bring the same commitment I had as a rider."Anastopoulos, also a former professional rider, is perhaps best known as the coach who oversaw Mark Cavendish’s return to winning form during the sprinter’s second spell with Soudal-QuickStep. He then went with Cavendish when he moved to the Astana team, and guided the sprinter to his 35th and record-breaking Tour de France stage win.He joins Netcompany from the Kazakh team, where he’s been head of performance since 2023, and will join the team’s coaching staff in a "senior role".Finally, Prof. Jeukendrup joins the team as director of physiology and nutrition after a career working in high performance sport, including across multiple sports as performance manager with the Dutch TeamNL and two years as director of sport strategy at Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, a role he left last month.It’s been a busy week for Netcompany Ineos, who first announced that former Tour de France and Giro d’Italia winner Egan Bernal extended his contract, apparently until the end of 2029. Then, hours after that announcement, they revealed seven other current riders were staying with the British outfit, with Connor Swift, Ben Swift’s cousin, committing until the end of the 2029 season as well. The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Yankee Birthday of the Day: Bullet Joe Bush
item.author: Matt Ferenchick
item.content:encoded: A good chunk of the heroes from Yankees history are one-team players who spent their entire careers in the Bronx. I’m talking Lou Gehrig, Joe DiMaggio, and Mickey Mantle to modern ones like Derek Jeter and Aaron Judge.However, it’s somewhat well known that the first couple decades in franchise history weren’t very successful. When the Yankees did finally reach the mountain top in 1923, the roster — including Babe Ruth — had a lot of key players who had notable runs elsewhere that had been acquired through trades.One of that list includes Bullet Joe Bush, who would be celebrating a birthday today.Leslie Ambrose “Bullet Joe” Bush November 27, 1892 (Ehime, MN) November 1, 1974 (Fort Lauderdale, FL) 1922-24Bush was born in Minnesota in 1892, one of seven children. He was dubbed “Joe” as a child, although the Bullet part of his nickname wasn’t added until his baseball career, as you might expect. As a child, Bush was said to practice his pitching by throwing “rotten apples through a crescent-shaped hole of a neighboring outhouse.”He began playing more organized baseball for the Brainerd, MN town team when he was 13 years old. Originally, Bush played third base. However, he was converted to a pitcher after the team captain noticed the speed at which his throws came in at. That’s when he truly began to get noticed, and a Montana-based minor league team eventually signed him when Bush was 18.In Montana, Bush’s manager was Cliff Blankenship, who had been credited for discovering Hall of Fame pitcher Walter Johnson. Blankenship mentored Bush before recommending him to Philadelphia Athletics’ manager Connie Mack. The A’s legend took his advice, and Bush was soon making his MLB debut as a 19-year old in August 1912.In 1913, A’s ace Jack Coombs missed most of the season with an illness, which led to Bush getting a more prominent role for the team. His numbers on the whole weren’t spectacular, but he went 15-6 for Philadelphia as they won the AL pennant. In the World Series, Bush was entrusted to start Game 3, and allowed just two runs (one earned) in a complete game victory over the Giants. The series was tied going into Game 3 and Philadelphia rode that win to take the series in five.After that season, Bush became a fixture in the A’s rotation. It took until 1916 for his rate stats like ERA to become genuinely good, but he did help Philadelphia make it back to the World Series in 1914, although they were swept by the Braves.However, as Bush began to become an excellent pitcher, the A’s team began to become way less than excellent. With the introduction of the rebel Federal League, Mack began to sell away players from that 1913 World Series-winning team rather than get into bidding wars, including Home Run Baker to the Yankees. It was hardly all his fault, but Bush ended up suffering a league-leading 24 losses in 1916.Eventually, Bush became part of the A’s sell-off and he was sent to the Red Sox in December 1917. In Boston, Bush immediately turned in one his best seasons to date in 1918, helping the Red Sox to the World Series. Boston ended up beating the Cubs in six games in the series. Bush lost his only start in Game 2, but he came out of the bullpen in Game 4. A still-pitching Babe Ruth was nursing a one-run lead going into the ninth but allowed the first two runners to reach. Bush came in and got a bunt force out at third and a double play to seal a 3-2 win. That gave Boston a crucial 3-1 lead in the series.An arm injury forced Bush to miss almost all of the 1919 season, but he came back in 1920 armed with a new weapon. During his return from injury, Bush stumbled across the forkball, which he is credited with inventing. While he was only okay in 1920, by 1921 he had mastered the pitch and was back to his best.However once again, financial concerns soon led to the breakup of a World Series-winning team Bush was on. Red Sox owner Harry Frazee began selling off players from that 1918 team. Many of those deals saw Red Sox stars going to the Yankees, most notably Ruth. Bush eventually became part of that list as he, fellow pitcher Sad Sam Jones, and shortstop Everett Scott were traded to New York in December 1921.Once again though, Bush joined a team on the brink of success. Thanks in part to Bush’s 26 wins, the Yankees won the AL pennant in 1922, although they fell to the Giants in the World Series. However the following year, Bush pitched a team-high 275.2 innings, helping the team back to the World Series. This time they emerged victorious, besting the Giants in six games. Bush himself got dinged with a loss in Game 1 despite allowing only one run in 6.2 innings out of the bullpen. In Game 5, he again came up big in the Fall Classic, allowing just one run in a complete game, giving the Yankees a 3-2 lead in the series. They clinched the franchise’s first championship the following day.Bush had a down season in 1924 as the Yankees failed to make it back to the World Series. The team opted to trade him to the St. Louis Browns for fellow pitcher Urban Shocker. Bush became a bit of a journeyman after that, playing for several teams before ending his MLB career back with the A’s in 1928.After a couple more years playing in the minors, Bush transitioned to coaching and led the Allentown Buffaloes to the Eastern League pennant in 1930. After leaving baseball, Bush held a variety of jobs before retiring to Florida, where he lived until passing away in 1974.Bullet Joe Bush is one of just two dozen or so players to have won a World Series championship with three different teams. He also came up remarkably big in all of those championships too.See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here.

item.title: Apple AirPods Pro 3 hit their lowest-ever price this Black Friday in the UK and US
item.author: Emily Tillett
item.content:encoded: If you're already invested in the Apple ecosystem, AirPods are a natural choice if you're after some brilliant headphones for on and off the bike. And if you already own a pair, you'll know just how good they are.The latest Pro 3 AirPods are one of our best headphones for cycling and are currently at their best-ever price for Black Friday in the UK and US. For UK shoppers, the Black Friday discount drops them by 29%, down to just £155.98, a huge £63 off the list price. And at Amazon US, the Airpods Pro 3 have an incredible $100 off, bringing the price down to just $149.These discounts really do make them a genuine deal, beating the previous lowest prices we've seen.Other AirPods models are also discounted, including the AirPods 5, which offer a different, open-ear design while retaining many of the features that make Apple's earbuds so popular.The Pro 3s take everything up a notch with an extremely impressive battery life, exceptional noise cancellation (and transparency mode) and sublime sound quality. Snap up this lowest-ever price whilst you can. View DealIf the AirPods Pro 3 are a little more than you need, Apple also has the AirPods 5 with an open-ear design while retaining many of the features of the Pro 3s. View DealWith 40% off and $100 in savings, the AirPods Pro 3 offer higher-end performance than the standard AirPods, while the added heart-rate monitoring feature makes them an even better-value buy.View DealThe standout deal is undoubtedly the AirPods Pro 3, with Black Friday discounts bringing them to only slightly more than the AirPods 5.The main difference between the two is their fit, noise cancellation, battery life and additional health features. Both use Apple's H2 chip and support features such as Adaptive Audio and Transparency, but the AirPods Pro 3 are the more feature-packed option.The AirPods Pro 3 use an in-ear design with five sizes of silicone tips, creating a seal that helps deliver stronger noise cancellation. They do also feature a 'Transparency' mode, which is great for cycling as it lets in surrounding noise. One of the big selling points on launch was the fact that the Pro 3s have a heart rate tracker, which on testing, was at least as accurate as a wrist-based sensor on a Garmin running watch. The catch here is that you can't use the Airpods as a standalone heart rate monitor in the traditional sense, they work with the Apple Fitness app only. The AirPods 5, meanwhile, have an open-ear design without silicone tips, making them a good alternative if you find in-ear earbuds uncomfortable or prefer to remain more aware of your surroundings. If you're already invested in the Apple ecosystem (like me), the seamless switching between devices is hard to beat, and both models are solid options.If sound quality is your top priority, the Technics EAH-AZ100 are another excellent option. We rated them highly in our testing, and they're currently 31% off on Amazon, down to £179.If you're shopping on a tighter budget, our top-rated budget cycling headphones are also on sale, with the Skullcandy option available for less than £20 on Amazon.Below, you'll also find the best Apple AirPods prices from other retailers, relevant to your location.

Whoop is a fitness band that first launched over a decade ago with elite athletes in mind, but has since become a popular choice for anyone looking to better understand their training, recovery, sleep and overall health. The Oura Ring takes a slightly different approach, packing its sensors into a ring that monitors sleep, activity, heart rate and recovery around the clock. It's particularly appealing if you want detailed health insights without wearing a watch or fitness band.Both are currently discounted on Amazon, with $100/£100 off the Oura Ring and up to $60/£60 off a new Whoop. It's currently discounted to $175.View DealUK shoppers can also save £60 on WHOOP Life, with the deal including the MG wearable device and a full 12-month membership.View DealThe Whoop Peak is reduced by £40 in the UK, making it a cheaper way to access its additional Healthspan, health and stress monitoring features.View DealThe Whoop is best described as a wearable health and fitness tracker. Many people liken it to a smartwatch, and the 4.0 model currently features in our guide to the .The Oura on the other hand is a smart ring. Worn on your finger like a regular ring, it can track more than 50 health metrics including heart rate, body temperature, sleep stages, menstrual cycles, and even aspects of your diet if you choose to. As mentioned, both are subscription based products are Whoop offers three subscription tiers, each providing a different level of tracking and insight.One includes the 5.0 device and core sleep, strain and recovery tracking. Peak builds on this with Healthspan features, including an estimate of your 'Whoop Age', plus health and stress monitoring. At the top of the range, Life comes with the MG device, adding ECG and blood pressure insights.Whether you're looking to upgrade your current fitness tracker or to finally give data-driven health and recovery tracking a try, these Black Friday deals offer a great opportunity to get started for less.Below, you'll also find the best Whoop and Oura Ring prices from other retailers, relevant to your location.

item.title: Marquez fastest in his final MotoGP Friday practice session
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Marquez, who stunned the MotoGP paddock by suddenly announcing his retirement at the outset of the day, outpaced '26 title rival Marco Bezzecchi by a quarter of a second with a late burst of speed in the hour-long afternoon session.He headed an Aprilia 2-3-4, with Bezzecchi narrowly leading the Trackhouse pair of Ai Ogura and Raul Fernandez.The 0.247s between Marquez in first and Bezzecchi in second was more than the gap between Bezzecchi in second and team-mate Jorge Martin in 10th place, Martin just sneaking into an automatic Q2 spot on Saturday at the expense of former team-mate Johann Zarco (who had a fast crash late on but was unhurt).Ducati-bound KTM rider Pedro Acosta, who will be expected to spearhead Ducati next year following Marquez's sudden retirement, was fifth (his lap set shadowing Martin), with stand-in Pol Espargaro using Acosta as a reference to place seventh and also secure a Q2 spot.There were also Q2 spots for Alex Marquez (despite a crash), Fermin Aldeguer and Fabio Di Giannantonio (despite an apparent bike failure).Both Acosta and KTM stablemate Brad Binder had crashes, Binder ending up well outside the top 10.

item.title: F1 Qatar GP: Antonelli leads Russell in opening practice
Cobbled Classics reveal revamped routes as E3 Saxo Classic and Dwars door Vlaanderen make changes for 2027
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: The pair are among the most important races of the March-April Classics block, both falling in the week before the Tour of Flanders along with In Flanders Fields, as well as being WorldTour and Women's WorldTour races in their own right.On Thursday, organisers of the E3 Saxo Classic presented their race's new look for its 70th edition on March 26, 2027.The race will be slightly shortened from 208.8km to 207.8km, while the number of climbs in the race has also been reduced, with 14 climbs featuring rather than 16. Organisers enacted the latter change after requests from riders and teams."We received a request from the peloton to adjust the course in terms of elevation gain. Our E3 DNA remains the same. It remains an attractive course. We still seek out cobblestone sections and steep climbs. That remains identical," Seppe Seynhaeve of the race organisation told .For the most part, the route of the E3 Saxo Classic – which starts and ends in Harelbeke – will be the same as the 2026 edition, with the brutal hill zone in the second half retaining the two ascents of the Oude Kwaremont as well as the Taaienberg, Eikenberg, Paterberg, and Tiegemberg, among others.The two climbs cut from the route will be the Berg Ten Stene and Oude Kruisberg, which lay after 85km and 108km in the 2026 race. 14 named climbs – among many other smaller ones – and nine cobbled sectors remain on the route.In contrast to the E3 Saxo Classic, the next edition of Dwars door Vlaanderen will be tougher than the last.The 81st edition of the men's race, which falls on March 31 next year, will feature 16 climbs, up from 12 in the 2026 edition. The Kluisberg climb is in for the Volkegemberg, while the trio of the Berg Ten Houte, Knokteberg-Trieu, and Hotond will each be tackled three times rather than twice, as was the case in 2026.Two loops of those three climbs will come in the middle of the race, while the final 72km remain unchanged. The race will run for 185km from Roeselare to Waregem."We have strengthened our DNA. We are adding the Kluisberg, which replaces the Volkegemberg, and we will cross the Trieu three times," Pavel Desmet, chairman of the KSV Waregem Vooruit, told .The women's race, meanwhile, will be run for the 15th time next spring with a 130km route starting and ending in Waregem.A more challenging route awaits the women's peloton, too, with 11 climbs on the menu, up from eight climbs this year. The race will feature a new loop of the Knokteberg-Trieu, Hotond, and Mariaborrestraat, while the final 72km will be identical to the men's Dwars door Vlaanderen."The riders will be presented with 130km featuring eleven climbs and six cobblestone sections along the way. Just like with the men, the Hellestraat – Kluisberg duo forms the gateway to the Flemish Ardennes." Desmet said of the women's race.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. Subscribe for unlimited access to our comprehensive news coverage, industry-leading CN Labs testing, expert columnists, and so much more. Plus, the Cyclingnews app means you can stay up-to-date wherever you go!

item.title: What happened in 2026 F1 Qatar GP first practice
item.author: Ben Anderson
item.content:encoded: New Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli comfortably set the pace in first practice for the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, despite failing to complete a clean quick lap on the softest tyre compound.As per usual, medium Pirelli tyres were favoured for the early running in FP1 and Antonelli worked his way down from a 1m25.0s to a 1m24.0s and finally to a 1m23.127s best, which surprisingly stood as the session’s fastest time, regardless of track improvement and everyone using the soft tyre.Antonelli attempted a soft tyre run of his own but had to abandon the lap after an oversteer moment. He ended the session 0.507s up on Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who found only 0.25s on the softs compared to his best lap on the medium tyre.Isack Hadjar continued his impressive recent form by setting the third fastest time for Red Bull, ahead of McLaren duo Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who according to Sky F1 both ran with an older specification of floor in this session.They were separated by just 0.01s and ended the session more than eight tenths off the pace.Max Verstappen rounded out the top six, 0.916s off, after encountering traffic through the final corner on his best lap. He also suffered more Red Bull radio problems in this session and complained of needing an impossible 10 more clicks of front wing angle to counter the car’s chronic understeer, while Hadjar lated reported feeling as though his car's front wing wasn't attached such was the lack of front grip.The Ferraris were well off the pace in seventh and eighth, Charles Leclerc 1.256s slower than Antonelli's benchmark and 0.102s clear of team-mate Lewis Hamilton.Arvid Lindblad’s Racing Bulls was the quickest of the midfield cars in ninth, a tenth down on Hamilton’s Ferrari and almost three tenths up on Pierre Gasly’s Alpine, which rounded out the top 10.1 Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) 1m23.219s2 George Russell (Mercedes) +0.467s3 Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) +0.661s4 Lando Norris (McLaren) +0.896s5 Oscar Piastri (McLaren) +0.966s6 Max Verstappen (Red Bull) +0.978s7 Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) +1.258s8 Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) +1.358s9 Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) +1.386s10 Pierre Gasly (Alpine) +1.557s11 Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) +1.838s12 Franco Colapinto (Alpine) +1.957s13 Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) +2.238s14 Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) +2.338s15 Rafael Camara (Haas) +2.438s16 Alex Albon (Williams) +2.475s17 Ollie Bearman (Haas) +2.548s18 Carlos Sainz (Williams) +2.779s19 Jak Crawford (Aston Martin) +3.081s20 Lance Stroll (Aston Martin) +3.188s21 Sergio Perez (Cadillac) +3.645s22 Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) +3.852s
