item.title: Yankees Potential Free Agent Target: Seiya Suzuki
item.author: Peter Brody
item.content:encoded: The hot stove has combusted into an inferno with less than a week to go before the expiration of the CBA at 11:59 pm ET on December 1st. Tarik Skubal was the first domino to fall, igniting a flurry of subsequent moves that has seen teams guarantee well over $1 billion in a three-day span. The Yankees, meanwhile, prefer to wade in the shallow end of the pool, committing modest outlays for relievers Jonathan Loáisiga, Tim Hill, and Brent Suter after receiving confirmation that closer David Bednar would return on the qualifying offer. There have been only wisps of smoke behind rumors linking them to additions on the position player side, recent comments from Brian Cashman hinting at a level of comfort to run it back with the in-house offense yet again. While corner outfield is certainly not an area of need, Seiya Suzuki represents one of the best available bats in a barren class of free agent hitters.143 games, 634 PA, .270/.368/.473, 26 HR, 31 doubles, 86 RBI, 131 OPS+, 134 wRC+, 14 DRS, +5 OAA, 4.5 fWAR, 5.1 rWAR2026 FanGraphs Depths Charts Projections: 149 games, 644 PA, .256/.346/.448, 24 HR, 30 doubles, 82 RBI, 120 wRC+, 2.7 fWARAt the beginning of the week, my colleague John analyzed Randy Arozarena’s prospective free agent fit. It is actually uncanny how similar the two corner outfielders profile to each other. The pair were born within six months of each other and have generally been well below average with the glove (2026 notwithstanding in Suzuki’s case). They both hit 26 home runs in 2026, sport a 128 wRC+ for their careers, and posted nearly identical triple-slash lines — .270/.368/.473 from Suzuki and .281/.381/.484 from Arozarena. FanGraphs Depth Charts projects nearly identical outcomes for the pair in 2027 — a 120 wRC+ and 30 doubles for each and a rounding error difference in home runs and fWAR. Arozarena will steal you more bags while Suzuki is a slightly surer bet in the field.Suzuki has been a remarkably consistent threat on offense since coming over from NPB prior to the 2022 season. Not including that debut season where he was limited to 111 games by injury, Suzuki has appeared in at least 130 games, hit at least 20 home runs, walked over ten percent of the time, and posted a wRC+ above 120 in each of the last four seasons. His pitch recognition is impressive, placing him at or above the 90th percentile in walk and chase rates. He does most of his damage against the fastball — particularly those on the inner half that he can pull in the air — but more than holds his own against off-speed pitches like the changeup and splitter.This season was a both a career year and a weird outlier campaign of sorts. He posted a career high 4.5 fWAR thanks largely in part to his first ever above-average season on defense — he generally is among the league leaders when it comes to the value he produces with his arm strength and accuracy but typically grades out as slightly below average overall until experiencing a massive improvement in his reaction time in 2026. That being said, Suzuki also regressed in key offensive areas. This season saw him lose about three mph in average and max exit velocity and was the first season since his rookie year that he posted a sub-40-percent hard-hit rate and a sub-.400 expected wOBA on contact despite his average bat speed remaining stable. He has also appeared in over 150 games just once in five seasons and you can likely bake in about a month of missed games given his history with knee, neck, and oblique injuries.I’m not sure how much I buy the improvement with the glove. That a trio of free agent position players in Suzuki, Brandon Lowe, and Luis Arraez posted their first ever solid defensive seasons on the cusp of or well into their thirties says as much about the noise and fickle nature contained within current defensive metrics as it does any tangible improvements in their defensive capabilities. Projections systems unanimously expect each of the three to regress back closer to their career norms going forward, which relegates Suzuki from All-Star level to solid starter level. It is hard to see the fit on the Yankees roster. Most projections expect Suzuki to sign in the neighborhood of four years and $100 million. New York already has over $80 million committed to their corner outfielders in 2028. They need a starter in center with Cashman noncommittal on Spencer Jones’ grasp on the job. Suzuki has just 133.2 innings of major league experience in left field under his belt, so you would be asking him to effectively learn a new position in the more difficult Yankee Stadium left field while sliding the best defensive left fielder in MLB in Cody Bellinger over to center, where he’s been merely average since 2020. As much as the Yankees would benefit from slotting his power righty bat into the middle of their lineup, they are better saving their likely limited funds for more pressing needs in center and in the infield. See more potential Yankees free agent targets here.

item.title: Black Friday smart trainer deals 2026: Upgrade your indoor cycling set-up with a top spec turbo
item.author: Paul Norman
item.content:encoded: If finding a decent day to ride outdoors is a challenge, upgrading your indoor training setup may be the solution.Smart trainers which hook up to Zwift and other indoor training apps are a hot item this Black Friday, with some nice discounts on everything from budget smart trainers to sophisticated indoor bikes. There are discounts too on many of the accessories that you need to complete your indoor setup, including many options for Zwift Cog and Click virtual shifting.We've searched out the best deals on indoor training hardware this Black Friday, so if you're looking for an indoor upgrade, take a look at our picks below. Wahoo continues to promote its Kickr Core 2, both as a stand-alone product and with Zwift Cog and Click. Arguably, the version with cassette offers more flexibility, as you can use it with different indoor apps. It's not going to break the bank to add Zwift Cog and Click this Black Friday either - see the offer below. It's also a good bet if you have multiple bikes you want to use with your trainer, as it's compatible with any drivetrain from eight to 12 speeds.View DealThe Zwift Upgrade Kit allows you to convert your trainer to single sprocket, saving wear on your drivetrain and freeing up a cassette. Check on Zwift's site that you trainer is compatible though, as many older models are not. There's a handy dropdown selector to confirm.View DealThe Elite Tuo bucks the trend to direct drive trainers. It's still smart, but one of the few wheel-on designs available. This makes it very compact, so it's a good option for small spaces and if you want to take your trainer to events for warm-ups.View DealThe Tacx Neo 2T is a worthy competitor to Wahoo's indoor training dominance, with a true direct drive design - no belts or chains - and resistance from 32 neodymium magnets.Tacx's design allows the Neo 2T to simulate cobbles and gravel, offering a change from tarmac and a more realistic ride feel through the Zwift jungle.View DealWahoo's Kickr Headwind fan is clever. Not only will it generate airspeeds of over 30mph, you can connect it to your training outfit wirelessly, so the wind speed increases as your virtual speed does. It will take a feed from an HRM too and blow harder as you do. It's a division up from a standard floor fan.View DealElite's training desk gives you a space to perch your tablet or laptop when running a training app. It's wheeled, so it's easy to move around and height adjustable to suit your preferred device height. View DealThis allows you to leave your outdoor bike outdoors and cuts down on set-up time. The frame can be adjusted quickly to suit different riders and V2 has adjustable crank length, so you can experiment with pro-style shorter cranks.View DealEven over a decade since its launch, the Wahoo Kickr is still one of the best smart trainers available. Now on V6, it offers WiFi connectivity and Race Mode for fast data transfer. Available either with Zwift Cog and Click or an 11-speed cassette, it's more affordable than ever too.View DealIf you fancy the fore and aft motion of the Kickr Move, this may be the last chance to buy, as Wahoo has discontinued its premium trainer. It's still a step up in price from the Kickr, but might address saddle discomfort suffered when changing speed. View DealAs the ultimate indoor training upgrade, the Kickr Bike Pro tilts, so you get a real climbing feel and work the muscles you'd use outdoors. Wahoo fits the bike with a Fizik Aliante R5 saddle and Fizik bar tape for a ride feel that's even more like your outdoor bike.View DealElite's Nero rollers have smart resistance, so you can hook them up to your training app for a ride that's more of a challenge than on a turbo. It should improve your balance and pedalling fluidity and the parabolic rollers reduce the risk of riding off the edge.View DealWahoo's Kickr Run offers hands-free speed adjustment, so no more falling off the back of your treadmill when you slow down suddenly. It hooks into the usual suspects, so you can see Watopia from a different angle.View DealIt's still a great trainer and a worthy upgrade over the Core 2, thanks to a heavier flywheel, steeper gradient simulation, higher resistance, the ability to rock with your efforts and fold-away legs.View DealThe Tacx Neo 2T trainer is available either with Zwift Cog and Click or, for the same price, with a freehub (but not a cassette). Its direct drive system means no belts internally and allows you to ride on simulated cobbles and gravel, as well as tarmac. Sigma Sports' Black Friday discount brings the price below the Kickr too.View DealThe Van Rysel D100 trainer is probably the cheapest entry into indoor training. Its stats don't match pricier trainers - it can only simulate a 6% gradient, for example - but it's foldable. It also comes ready-fitted with Zwift Cog and Click, so it's ready to ride out of the box.View DealElite's trainers offer a dash of style and the Rivo has up to 2,000 watts resistance and can operate without mains power. It comes with pre-installed Zwift Cog and Click and can be used with 142mm thru-axles or quick release, with Boost and Super Boost adapters available.View DealThe Kickr Core 2 with Zwift Cog and Click allows you to leave your shifters alone, instead offering clunkless virtual shifting via its orange single sprocket. Not only is this quiet and fast, it also reduces chain wear, as there's a straight chainline. The Click shifters mount to your bars and also offer Zwift menu options. View DealIts 11-28 tooth range should be enough to handle the trainer's 16% max gradient, while allowing you to run down at speed when you hit its -10% diownhills.View DealOn the subject of climbs and descents, add the Kickr Climb to your setup and it will tilt your bike up when you hit a gradient. Not only does this make the effort of hitting a 20% climb more realistic, it engages the muscles you'd actually use in a climb, so you'll be better trained for when you hit one in the real world.View DealYou'll need a fan to go with that and the Kickr Headwind adds yet more realism as it can be linked wirelessly to your training setup to change its output as you ride faster or your heart rate increases. Wahoo says it can hit wind speeds of over 30 mph for a suitable blast when riding full gas.View DealWahoo has discontinued the Kickr Move, so if you want its fore and aft movement, alongside side-to-side, now may be one of your last opportunities to buy, particularly at a price that matches the Kickr V6. View DealZwift Ride V2 comes bundled with the Kickr Core 2 with this £200 Black Friday discount, offering a turnkey indoor smart bike set-up that's modular, so it's a little easier to move around than a one-piece indoor bike. Zwift Click shifters are built in and the V2 smart frame can fit a wider range of rider heights and is more easily adjustable than its predecessor, as well as supporting variable crank lengths. View DealIf you've got a smart trainer, but missed the Zwift Cog bandwagon, Zwift has a Black Friday offer that drops the UK price to just £12.50. Check your trainer and freehub for compatibility though, as older models may not be compatible.View DealWahoo is also selling its premium Kickr Bike Pro with a Black Friday discount. Since it tilts, it will simulate climbs more realistically than a bike-plus-trainer set-up and engage the muscles you'd use to climb outdoors.For the ultimate indoor training set-up, this is it, although you'll need a dedicated training space. You're not going to want to move its 40-plus kilograms around the house.View DealSigma Sports has a discount on the Kickr Bike Shift, which pares down the functionality of the Kickr Bike Pro for a more affordable dedicated indoor bike. It doesn't tilt, but the steel frame is narrower than the Pro's and its belt drivetrain is almost silent.View DealThe Wahoo Kickr Run's automatic speed adjustment makes speeding up or slowing down - or stopping - during your workout much easier than manual controls. It connects up to Zwift for a change of scenery from riding your bike through Watopia.View DealOur other Black Friday 2026 roundups👕 : With 25% off sitewide, we've rounded up our favourite items from the British brand.💾 : A live, ever-changing roundup of our favourite deals on Garmin's bike computers, smartwatches, heart rate monitors and more, from Garmin's own site and beyond.

item.title: We’ve tested these $8.99 Chinese aero socks and they’re faster than big brands and WAY cheaper too thanks to Black Friday markdowns
item.author: Emily Tillett
item.content:encoded: When it comes to marginal gains, even your socks can make a difference. Aero-specific designs are widely used by professional riders, but the fastest options often come with eye-watering price tags of $60 or more. We were intrigued to come across these Rockbros aero socks on Amazon this Black Friday where they are currently up to 50% off, with the biggest reductions depending on the size and colour you choose. With prices starting at just $8.99 in the US, these Rockbros aero socks cost a fraction of many premium alternatives, but that doesn't necessarily mean they've cut corners when it comes to performance, as we recently found out. The socks are also available at a discount in the UK in a selection of brighter colourways, while the white version remains a good-value option with an RRP of £14.99.We recently took 26 pairs of cycling socks to the wind tunnel for a to see just how much difference aero socks can make.These Rock Bros socks performed surprisingly well, finishing on the podium and beating several much more expensive options.The Rock Bros socks use a ribbed material on the upper, with a silicone band around the top and a thicker section under the foot. You can get them in sizes S, M and L, covering US shoe sizes 5-14 with plenty of colour and design options to choose from. We've yet to carry out a full review of these socks, but what we can say is that the feel and quality are comparable to many of the big-name brands, making them a tempting option at this price.If you're looking to add some aero gains, the Rockbros socks are well worth considering with prices as low as $8.99 in the US. That price is hard to argue with for impressive wind-tunnel results.

item.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘Sometimes your mind or your body just takes a second’
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: If you still have leftovers in the fridge, congratulations. That means you’ll be able to celebrate twice today.First, a Knicks win over the Heat. Then, feasting on another round of reheated turkey, mac and cheese, and mashed potatoes.Here’s yesterday’s post, slightly padded with a few more quotes.On the Knicks still having room for improvement:“I’ve said this before, we play so many games. You can never get too high. I guess we’re 12-3 since the start, but our [performance] does still stink. We haven’t arrived. We still have to embrace the little things.“They do this (points downward), but eventually they’re going to do this (points upward). When we do that, handling the challenges in front of us the right way is going to be big. You can’t get too high in this league because you’re that close to going the other way. Just like if you’re down, it’s not the end of the world; you’re that close to flipping it. So you try to stay even-keeled and kind of stick with your process, especially if it’s something that you believe in. And we believe in it. Eventually things are going to change or turn in the right direction.”On Jordan Clarkson being instrumental in establishing the Knicks’ flexible bench rotation and wanting him to remain with the organization beyond his playing career:“As a coach, you could want to do that, but you have to have others around you that will at least support it initially to see how it turns out. And a huge, huge, huge catalyst for that was Jordan Clarkson. Jordan Clarkson was the one, if you’re talking about giving 100 percent out there to what allows me to do that, I think Jordan Clarkson gave me at least 90 percent of the opportunity to do it, because here’s an accomplished veteran that could be in the rotation for almost any team out there, let alone a championship team, and I can literally play him six straight games and then sit him 10 straight games and he’s gonna be the same dude every fricken’ day. And he’s gonna talk the same way to his teammates. Not ‘can you believe what Mike Brown did?’ Nah, he’s gonna be the same dude, uplift the group, and then when I call his number again, he’s gonna be ready to go. He’s a guy that, even when he gets done playing, it’s one of those things where you hope that he can just be a part of this organization in some way, shape or form until he doesn’t want to be part of this organization. He’s that type of person, in my opinion.”On the benefits of potentially missing the NBA Cup knockout rounds:“It is important (to win and potentially advance), but the reality of it is, when you look at the schedule, and you see that our percentage [to advance] is not that high, and so they kind of shared with me what our schedule would look like if we don’t go and if we do go. And you look at it, you’re like, ‘Whoa, that’s a lot of days off if you don’t go.’ And so again, you want to compete; you want to win. But if you don’t, in my opinion, when you look at the schedule… you’re like, there’s an opportunity if you got some guys banged up to get rest and/or to work on some things in between the games that you have if you’re not involved in the Cup.”On the physical and mental toll of competing in the NBA Cup:“I didn’t really break it down to an 83rd game, but when I talk about the Cup, it adds a level of stress maybe on your mind and your body because the games are intense as you go along and you’re playing more games in a short amount of time.“I remember it was like, game, game, game, and then you win the Cup, and you celebrate it that night, and you hop on a plane and go play in Indiana the next night. And so it’s great. You like the competition and the setup, but it adds a lot of stress to you physically and mentally. I’m saying this because especially with the extended season we had last year and how taxing the games were for our playoff run mentally and physically, I’m trying to be smart, so if — knock on wood — we end up advancing, I’ll try to be smart about it.”On refusing to chase regular-season wins at all costs and learning from Golden State’s 73-win season:“I try not to chase wins, especially early in the season. You want to win, but I’m not going to win every game at all costs.“I wasn’t part of the staff [for the first Golden State title] [Golden State] won Steve [Kerr’s] first year. Then they lost in the second year, but they set a regular season record of 73 wins, and one of the things that he used to tell me, they gassed themselves trying to get this record and come playoff time they just didn’t have enough in the tank to close it. And so that always sits right here for me.”On calling Pacôme Dadiet into his office and threatening to remove him from the rotation over his lack of effort:“I didn’t think he played hard in the game before. And I actually called him into my office and showed him some film. I told him, ‘As a young guy, if you don’t play hard, I can’t play you.’“And I said, ‘Believe me, I got a lot of guys I can go to. I’m not afraid to go to somebody else. So the least you could do is play hard.’ And I showed him how he wasn’t. And I thought [Wednesday], he played hard.”On leaving OG Anunoby’s injury management to the medical staff:“There are a lot of medical terms that are above my head. They tell me and I don’t really pick up on the injury. If he’s out, I change my minutes sheet. And then I’ll just wait for them to tell me when he’s back. [Wednesday], OG’s individual work happened before shootaround and I didn’t even know he had individual work until his player development guy told me later on. You never want a guy to hurt himself more. But I don’t think about it.”On the Knicks still having plenty of room for improvement despite winning 12 of their last 15 games:“We’re 12-3 since the start, but our s–t still does stink. We haven’t arrived, and we still have to embrace the little things.”On the Knicks never panicking after their 0-3 start and gradually finding their rhythm:“I don’t think we had any panic. It wasn’t like we started 0 and 3 and we were getting blown out by 15 and 20 every game. It was a possession game each of those three losses and could’ve gone either way. So we knew that, and we knew it was just a play here or a play there that could’ve changed the game. We just tried to make sure we’re focusing on every possession. Sometimes your mind or your body just takes a second at the beginning of the season. I feel like we’re in a good space, physically and mentally, continuing to get better. Really diving into our core principles.”On Brown experimenting with an unusually deep rotation against Cleveland:“I looked at the bench in the first quarter and realized, ‘Wow, we played like 10 people in that first quarter.’”On the Knicks’ supporting cast stepping up and trusting Karl-Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson as their leaders:“I mean, it’s big for our team. Those guys [Towns and Brunson] are going to carry us enough, so today obviously it was an all-around game. We’re always going to have their backs, and they always have ours, and it just shows you what type of team we are. It could be anybody on any night, but they’re going to carry us to the promised land.”On Clarkson encouraging Pacôme Dadiet and reminding his teammates to stay ready:“JC is always big on that, telling guys to stay ready. He was in [Dadiet’s] ear the whole shootaround [Wednesday morning]. Just telling everybody to stay ready because you never know when your name is called.”On endorsing Tom Thibodeau as a potential head coaching hire for struggling NBA franchises:“I made three playoffs with Thibodeau as my coach so his track record is one of success. So of course if I was a team that wanted to get back on track, I’d look at Tom Thibodeau to be my coach.”On Thibodeau’s tactical knowledge, dedication and ability to prepare his teams to win:“It’s the X’s and O’s and the amount of care he puts into his craft, his team. He steps into that gym every day and, you know, you can say anything you want about the way he coaches, but one thing I know is his team is prepared to win a game. So that’s a testament to who he is as a coach, the preparation he puts his team through and also his ability to have his team ready for the moment.”On the Knicks’ bench players embracing fluctuating minutes and not having egos:“We care about each other. We want to win for each other. We’re willing to take on different roles and we know that we’ve got each other’s back. If Jose’s got it going and my minutes are shortened, awesome. And vice versa. All of us, Deuce [McBride] included in that, I would throw him in that as well, all of us kind of feel that way. That’s really cool.“I’ve been saying it, I’ve been a broken record about it, but you don’t see that — that’s very rare where no ego or ulterior motives get involved. That’s something special that you want to be a part of.”

item.title: Black Friday Garmin deals: Massive savings on Edge computers, smartwatches, power meters and more
item.author: thomas.wieckowski@futurenet.com (Tom Wieckowski)
item.content:encoded: It's arrived! Black Friday is officially here, and the Black Friday Garmin deals are in full swing, with crazy cheap prices across smartwatches, bike computers, and more. In curating this page, we'll sift through them all, weed out the bad ones, and collate together all the deals we'd be happy to buy ourselves. We'll also bring in deals from Garmin's subsidiaries, such as Tacx smart trainers, TrainingPeaks software, and more. Garmin launched three new products this autumn, the Edge 1060, Explore 3 and Explore 3 Plus. As a result, we're hoping / expecting to see a few of the older ones come down to their best-ever prices. We're also looking out for Fenix and Epix deals in the smartwatch space, and have plenty of tools at our disposal to find when something hits a new low price. The Fenix 8 is 25% off; the cheapest it has ever been on Amazon. There are also five versions to choose from in the 47mm face size variant. The entry-level Forerunner 70 has a nice 20% knocked off in a range of colours. You can still use recovery insights and training plans with this watch, and it has built-in GPS to track your running pace and splits. View DealCurrently at its lowest-ever price, the 265 will cover all of your running needs. You can also use Spotify to take care of your music, as well as just using it as a cool everyday watch. View DealThe popular Forerunner 970 smartwatch is 13% off in three different colours. This premium running- and triathlon-focused smartwatch is geared to help you run and also provides HRV status and sleep metrics. This bundle deal from Garmin also comes with a Power Bank included to help with charging when needed.View DealThe Edge Explore 3 may have arrived, but the Explore 2 is still available and is a good option for riders prioritising navigation features without a lot of other bells and whistles. The Edge 540 is 14% off right now, though it was available for $244 last November so we expect this to come down more over the weekend. View DealThe Edge 840 is at its lowest price in 30 days on Amazon right now, though it has been on sale for less cash this year. Officially, this unit has been superceded by the 850, but it's still a very capable unit with a touchscreen. View DealThe Edge 550 is on sale right now with a healthy 26% off. This is a mighty computer, but we felt the lack of a touchscreen limited it slightly. If you are happy with buttons, take a look. The Edge 850 is also on sale, discounted by 17%. In essence, this is the 550 with a touchscreen. It's a slightly bigger unit with a touchscreen, a built-in speaker and all the usual Garmin training and fitness tools. View DealThe Garmin Edge 1050 is a top-tier Garmin unit and is arguably still worth buying over the recently launched and more expensive Edge 1060. $100 off, this unit is a monster, with a brilliant, clear display and fast touchscreen. This unit pairs a rear light with a Bluetooth radar to help you monitor upcoming vehicles from up to 153 yards away. If you want a built-in camera too, scroll down. View DealThe Varia RCT715 is on sale in the US at 25% off. This unit brings together a camera, taillight and radar to help keep you safer on the bike. It Bluetooth-pairs with your head unit so you can view radar alerts.The Garmin Varia Vue is 27% off if you want to invest in front and rear Varia units. This camera/light pairs a 600-lumen front light with a 4K camera to capture your rides. Tip: You will need a Micro SD card for the unit too. View DealThe Flux 2 is discounted on the Garmin website; it's a solid smart trainer that prioritises low noise and is accurate within 2.5%. The trainer can connect with all the usual indoor training apps, so you can have a solid winter of riding. View DealThe Tacx Neo 2T with Zwift Cog and Click is 18% off right now. This top-level trainer comes with Zwift's Cog and Click sprocket pre-installed, plus clip-on virtual shifters, so you can use it easily with any bike. It also works without power in standalone mode, which is useful for races, events, or outdoor riding.View DealWant to go the whole hog with a premium smart bike? Th Neo Bike Plus has a 10% discount. This is a fully adjustable smart bike that aims to offer the ultimate immersion indoors. The trainer vibrates and simulates road surfaces; dynamic inertia tech makes it feel like an outdoor ride, and the built-in fans mimic wind and keep you cool. View Deal25% off a year's subscription to TrainingPeaks gives you the longstanding calendar and planning platform, workout builder software, connection to most popular bike computers, and now the TrainingPeaks Virtual indoor cycling app. View DealGarmin's latest RS210 power meter pedals are on sale. This deal is for the RS210 dual-sided SPD SL option which gained recharging capability over the previous units battery powered tech. SPD and SPD-SL pedal bodies can be switched onto the axles, and the pedals are accurate to within +/-1%. View DealThe single-sided Garmin Rally RS110 power meter pedals are 14% off in the Sigma sale. If you want to be able to swap your power meter easily between bikes, this is a good option for SPD-SL cleats.View DealThe Forerunner 55 is a nice entry point into the world of smartwatches and has a healthy discount in the black colour. This watch will suit runners, but will suit anyone just wanting a Garmin smartwatch with its two-week battery life. View DealThis deal sees the fēnix 8 drop to its lowest ever price on Amazon in the 47 mm/slate grey version. The fēnix 8 is a top-level smartwatch with voice control and contactless payment tech. Its AMOLED screen is punchy and vivid, yet you still get up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode. View DealThe Garmin Varia RCT715 is at 21% on Amazon; its discount has increased from 15% over the past few days. The RCT715 is a light, camera and rear radar in one and has daylight visibility up to a mile. The Edge Explore 2 is a more basic unit that prioritises mapping and navigation. It doesn't have as many bells and whistles, but if that's all you need, it's a solid buy.This is a really good price for the Garmin Edge 540. A solid little computer that's packed with a load of features. It doesn't have a touchscreen, so consider this point if it's a deal-breaker for you. The Edge 840 unit is just over 20% off and is available for under £300. This is a solid operator, but the Edge 850 which got an upgraded colour touschcreen is also on sale below. View DealHere's the solar-charging version of the Edge 840, also on sale with 25% off. If you live somewhere with lots of sunshine, this will be worth a look. I didn't find the solar tech too useful in the UK. The Garmin Edge 850 is also discounted by just under 20% in the Sigma sale. This unit has a colour touchscreen and has lots of advanced training features.View DealThis is a big saving on the Edge 1040 Solar, with over 25% off. In bright sunlight, we found it could go weeks without charging. Making it ideal for long rides or touring. Garmin's flagship model until the recent launch of the 1060, the 1050 is a powerhouse, with a built-in bell and contactless payment technology. It's packed with features; do you need them all? The discount has increased on this one, increasing from 10 to 17% since the sales began. Our other Black Friday 2026 roundups👕 : With 25% off sitewide, we've rounded up our favourite items from the British brand.💾 : A roundup of our favourite deals on Wahoo tech, such as smart trainers and bike computers, from Wahoo's own website and beyond.

item.title: These brilliant bike lights are the most eye-catching I've ever tested. You can now save up to 40% off the usual price in this Black Friday deal
item.author: Rich Owen
item.content:encoded: It almost goes without saying that being as visible as possible to other road users is vital to staying safe when out on your bike.With that in mind, I've been testing the latest Knog Cobber Reflex bike lights, they are seriously bright and have a 170-degree beam angle that gives a super-visible light spread. They've got some really cool and unique light modes too – more on them below.As it's Black Friday, I've been looking for some deals on the Cobber Reflex lights and have found savings on both the front and rear models. Here are the best prices I've found:The lights are ideal for urban riding as they're quick to remove and, measuring 60 (L) x 35 (W) x 25 (D) mm, are easily stashable in pockets or a bag. They have an IP67 rating, which means they are totally waterproof and dust-tight.Both front and rear lights have lots of light modes that not only look cool, but also boost your visibility.The Cobbers have high and low output settings, flashing modes, a pulsing mode where the light spreads from the centre to the edges, and Reflex mode where the light strobes in the direction your bike is leaning. The rear light also detects when you're braking and gets brighter.I like the pulsing light modes the best, possibly because they put me in mind of KITT from the '80s TV classic Knight Rider and the Cylons from Battlestar Galactica. The responsive Reflex mode is a really cool addition too.While I'm yet to try this feature, you have the ability to design your own light modes for the front Cobber Reflex by downloading Knog's ModeMaker 2.0 software to your computer.Both models use rubber straps for easy mounting, which also means you can run them on your headtube, seatpost, forks, bars, or seatstays. Run times range from 2.5 hours at max brightness, to 70 hours in eco-mode, charging is via USB-C.

item.title: Tadej Pogačar’s neo-pro salary revealed, as his agent details big rise in wages for young talents
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Tadej Pogačar's agent Alex Carera has revealed how the market for young riders has completely changed since the Slovenian turned pro back in 2019, with wages now eclipsing those Pogačar received.Speaking to , Carera said Pogačar's first professional contract, having won the Tour de l'Avenir and Giro della Regione Friuli-Venezia Giulia in 2018, saw him net a €60,000 pro contract.Now, eight years later, things are completely different, he said."Tadej's first professional contract involved an annual salary of €60,000, plus a bonus of €20,000 if he won the Tour de l'Avenir that year," Carera, co-head of the A&J Sports agency, told ."All young riders in those years signed their first professional contract for €70-90,000. Certainly not for more money."Today, riders in a similar position, such as those who have won the Tour de l'Avenir, stand to earn a lot more when they ascend to the WorldTour shortly afterwards.Joseph Blackmore, Paul Seixas and Lorenzo Finn stand among the recent winners of the French race, while Jarno Widar, Jakob Omrzel and Finn have won the past three editions of the Giro d'Italia Next Gen. All have top-level contracts heading into 2027."If you win the Tour de l'Avenir now, you sign for €300,000," Carera said.Budgets and wages have risen across the board since Pogačar turned pro, with median WorldTour team budgets rising from approximately €18 million to around €28 million between 2019 and 2025. In 2026, total team budgets topped €663 million, up by €33 million from 2025.As for Pogačar, it goes without saying that his pay has exploded given his on-bike success since that initial €60,000 contract. He now takes home a reported €8 million per year as the highest-paid rider in cycling.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. Plus, the Cyclingnews app means you can stay up-to-date wherever you go!

item.title: Five big revelations from Marquez's retirement announcement
item.author: Eden Hannigan
item.content:encoded: Marc Marquez’s MotoGP retirement announcement was stunning in itself, but the surprises kept coming as he revealed more about his decision timing, how he’d kept the secret and what had prompted it all.A special press conference was held at Valencia shortly after the weekend’s opening practice session (in which Marquez was narrowly pipped by vanquished 2026 title rival Marco Bezzecchi), with Marquez holding court initially in front of a room packed with the entire grid and scores of team personnel from across the paddock.He stopped proceedings to arrange a farewell photo with all the rest of the riders, so they could then go and get on with their practice day business.And then after that, the press conference got under way in earnest.Here are the key things Marquez revealed.Marquez opened his account in his exceptional press conference by admitting exactly when and where he had made the decision to retire: at the Japanese Grand Prix at the start of October.“My decision was done after Motegi,” Marquez revealed, also sharing that “the only person in the world [to] know was my brother Alex.”Nobody else knew prior to this week about his impending announcement either, as he only told his father, Julia, on Wednesday night, and his mum found out this morning, one hour before the announcement.Even Ducati was kept in the dark over the news, with Marquez revealing his plans to general manager Gigi Dall’Igna and other key personnel in the factory only set up on Thursday.Part of the reasoning over the secrecy was his closeness to his brother, but also because of the amount of energy it took to even speak about any kind of retirement. He was retiring regardless - win or loseRegardless of the outcome of the championship, Marquez says his mind was made up at Motegi, and that it “[didn’t] matter if I win or if I finish second or third.”After that weekend, he was two points shy of leader Jorge Martin, and 47 ahead of his Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi.Ever the pragmatist, Marquez followed his instincts to end his career now, adding that following his instincts has proven statistically smart in the past.Asked whether retirement had been a discussion before he spoke with his brother in Japan, he said: “No, because this is another thing. In the other times, 2023 was the only time. And I was discussing with my people, because I had doubts, because I felt like, ‘OK, I can do it again’.“But then we find the way, because in that moment, I need help from my people and my people, when I need help, they are always there.“But this time I was fully convinced, no discussion. I said to [Alex], it doesn't matter if I win or if I finish second or third. And at that time, the championship was very close.“But I say, ‘the correct thing, my instincts say, this is the way’. And most of the time in my career, when I follow my instincts, the statistics say that was the good way. So I follow the statistics.“But this time I'm more than convinced that that is the correct thing for my personal and professional life.” The injury that scares him most came backMarquez’s body has been through so many surgeries, even before the career-threatening 2020 injury and its complex, years-long repercussions, and the hugely significant Mandalika 2025 and Le Mans 2026 crashes.But amid all the many, many broken bones, it’s the bouts of double vision that have really scared him.And he revealed on Friday for the first time that they’d reoccurred in both his last major injuries and that this had made him worry for his quality of life beyond racing - and take more care for the rest of the season as a result.“Of course, you can work, of course, you can fight, I'm a fighter, but there's another point that I'm scared, and I start to feel the fear,” said Marquez.“And it's not the fear of the bikes, it's not the fear of the speed, it's an injury that is there, but at the moment, it's not affecting my personal and professional life.“After the Indonesian GP [in 2025], as part of my injury on the arm, I had double vision again, only for 48 hours.“After Le Mans, I had another double vision again, only for 12 hours.“Luckily, those two times I was able to recover well, and it was one of the main reasons why I controlled the risk, and why I crashed less this second part of the season.”Marquez had his first bout of double vision way back in his Moto2 days, following a heavy practice crash at Sepang in 2011 when he was challenging Stefan Bradl for the title as a rookie.He was sidelined for four months as a result, and required surgery before he could race again, but it didn’t stop him from returning and dominating Moto2 in 2012 then graduating straight to MotoGP and commencing his extraordinary run of immediate success there.It didn’t occur again until a training crash at the end of 2021, and then it flared up again very soon afterwards as a consequence of his horrendous Mandalika warm-up crash in early 2022.Having not happened for 10 years, for it to occur four times in the next five was clearly too disconcerting for Marquez. Go beyond the headlines and sign up to The Lean Angle, The Race's MotoGP newsletter. You'll get bespoke content direct to your inbox every Tuesday, plus the occasional one-off edition like today, where we had a special on the Marquez retirement news.How he handled racing with this secretAsked how he’d been able to focus on the five racing weekends he’d done since making his decision, amid the title fight too, Marquez said that was partly because “nobody knows, only Alex”.That meant he didn’t have to think or talk about it with the wider world.The other thing that helped him was a message from an unnamed “legend of MotoGP” who gave him the advice to “promise something to your body and your body will give extra”.From there on, Marquez said he would keep reminding himself that it would be the last time he would race at each of the venues, and that it gave him the extra drive and performance to make it through each weekend.He also addressed why he looked so “serious” after some of his sprint podiums, notably at Sepang where he seemed disappointed with a second-placed finish behind Pedro Acosta.It wasn’t because he was angry, “It was because I was suffering,” Marquez said. “I was suffering and the results covered my real situation.” Making big decisions in life always comes with some semblance of doubt.But for Marquez, his conclusions were clear - and crucially, made at a time where he was free from the worst of his injury woes.Asked by The Race whether he had second-guessed his choice at all in the weeks that followed, he said: "No, because as I always say, you cannot take any decision when you are injured or when you are on your peak of adrenaline. And then the decision I made when I was there alone in Twin Ring Motegi, I was quiet.“And in that weekend, I said, it's the time. Of course, there were some races that I was thinking. But then, yeah, I feel like it was the time, many things on the limit.“And we are humans. And as I say, I started to feel the fear. It didn't affect me, because then I have the capacity to fully concentrate.“But just to think about, again, double vision. Of course, in life, you have risk. But if you are competing, you have more risk.“So in the end, it's trying to understand all your situations, the amount of effort you put in your career, especially the last years, and life continues.“So this is the most important, and it's something that I understood in 2020 and 2021. Before that, I thought there was no life out of the paddock. There, I understand that life continues.”

item.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
item.content:encoded: A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News. Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney get details from Olivia Levieux, Markets Strategist with Bloomberg News (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'He's not a guy that just mails it in... he's always been a real killer in races' – Why George Bennett is backing Primož Roglič for 'special results' as former teammates reunite at NSN
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: When Primož Roglič was presented the option of NSN Cycling Team as an option to extend his career into 2027, who else was he going to call other than a former teammate of six seasons, George Bennett?Just six months apart in age, the New Zealand national champion raced as a GC domestique alongside Roglič for what was then LottoNL-Jumbo and then Jumbo-Visma. During those years together, Bennett was part of the winning team from Roglič's first of five Grand Tour triumphs at the 2019 Vuelta a España, but also took in the ultimate low of losing the 2020 Tour de France to Tadej Pogačar on the penultimate day, only for it to be followed by the ultimate bounce back at the subsequent Vuelta, where his new teammate claimed the second of his four red jerseys. Few riders have experienced the resilience of Roglič – which has made him so successful but also so compelling throughout his years in the peloton – first-hand like Bennet has, and the Kiwi isn't expecting him to slow down now that he's at NSN at 37."Well, I knew because he called me, and it was a very quick turnaround. We had a quick chat about the team and basically asked me to give him some pros and cons, and then within a couple of days it was announced, and it all went really fast," Bennett told on Wednesday when asked about how he experienced the surprise late transfer announcement. "Was I surprised? No, I mean, I guess I was surprised it happened so late in the piece. But early on, I thought that he would be a really good signing. I knew he was up and knew that Red Bull was not going to be a viable place for him to stay. "And I'd mentioned to them ages ago that he's not a guy that just mails it in and goes out for a contract; he's always been a real killer in races, and I don't really think he's slowing down. "He's not personally getting slower. It's just that there's been this revolution, and the rate of improvement of other guys has been exponential. And you have these young guys coming through at a crazy level, but I think actually this year there were times he was better than ever, and it just didn't line up that he got to show that in races. "Hit by a car before the Vuelta, and obviously team priorities at Red Bull, and there's a lot of things like that going on, so I think here in this environment with a team around him and everyone backing him, I think we'll still see a lot of pretty special results."Looking back on some of those Grand Tour victories as teammates from seven and six years ago, Bennett compared the jeopardy and occasional drama which has followed Roglič with that of another of his former teammates, and the Slovenian's compatriot, Pogačar. Roglič's incredibly successful career is one that has been marked by crashes and hardship, all of which he has come out the other side of to still be hitting out as one of the top riders in the world. Even this most recent season – one which almost saw him head into retirement before figuring out that he did want to continue and finding a place at NSN – was one where getting knocked off his bike by a driver almost derailed his main goal of racing the Vuelta, where he eventually finished an impressive second on the comeback from injury. "I think starting late, there's always a sense that it could go wrong as well," said Bennett, referring to Roglič's move across from ski jumping to road cycling. "There are these dramatic moments of just crashes and last-minute losses, but for me, what was so special early on is having a guy that could just – if you could get him close – he had this unbelievable finish on him. "I think he can fight like not many guys can, and can fight all the time, you know. Losing the Tour that year [in 2020], we got up and we won the Vuelta, and did it again the next year. "I think he appreciates the opportunity he has, and you know he'll just go to the end, especially if you do a job, and that's all you can ask as a helper. But there has always been a sense of sort of drama around him because as much as of the things that go right, there's also some of the things that go wrong – whereas someone like Tadej doesn't miss. Tadej is just knocking out win, win, win, win. There's less jeopardy in a way unless you're talking Roubaix or something; it's more of a guarantee."It's a kind of jeopardy that has made the flame burn even stronger for Bennett when it comes to motivation, wanting to ride to more successes with Roglič as they reunite as teammates."I think for me, having been with him for so long and being part of those losses, it kind of has given me a bit of a soft spot for him, that you know I want to step up again and try and remedy a few of the losses and try and get back those highs," he said.A new era of GC racing for NSNBennett is relishing the opportunity to race as a domestique deluxe for any of the new leaders into 2027, enjoying the team's shift after several recent years of operating as a mountain breakaway hunter."Oh, I love it. I mean, on a personal level, that's what I would say my expertise is: being a GC domestic. Being in bike races, I'm realistic now; I'm not winning these mountaintops anymore," said Bennet over a video call on Wednesday. "But it's still what I love doing, so to be part of a team with that in mind, it's a different mindset, and you have to be a bit more clinical. You have to know when to push, when not to push; there are so many aspects of riding GC, and it's not just climbing domestiques that we need; it's also the guys on the flat for staying out of trouble, and the whole approach has to change. It's less opportunistic, more methodical, and more like turning over every stone, and that trickles down to the whole team. "For me personally, it's what I love doing, and I think that's when I've been at my best as being a helper for these GC guys, and we've got Primož, but we've also got Richie, Buitrago, and Van Eetvelt, so I think I'm staring down the barrel of what's potentially a very busy year, but at the same time, it's very exciting."As a team who ranked 19th in the world last season with only 16 wins to their name, Bennett described how NSN have been able to celebrate big when things have paid off, but with a much-improved roster in 2027, those occasions may well become much more frequent. "I think for NSN the highs go really far – we haven't won a lot of races, and we weren't necessarily one of these huge teams, but now we kind of are, and some of the races I've won on this team with [Ethan] Vernon, with Brady [Gilmore], with Stevie [Williams], they feel like unbelievable because, like, holy shit, we won, and I think that's that's special," he said. "Now we have those same guys, but we also have some big champions to go with it." The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
item.author: Noah Shachtman, wired.com
item.content:encoded: The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else.Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”

item.title: Rabobank returns to title sponsorship as new naming sponsor of Visma-Lease a Bike Women
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: Visma-Lease a Bike have unveiled a new title sponsor for their women's team, with Rabobank making its return to a title sponsorship role after a 10-year absence. The team will officially be known as Rabobank-Lease a Bike Women’s Pro Cycling Team from 2027The Dutch bank, which pulled out of men's cycling at the end of 2012 – after a long sponsorship of this very team – and out of women's cycling at the end of 2026, has been investing again in the sport in recent years, but Friday's announcement marks a significant step back towards its prominence of old. Friday's announcement of Rabobank's sponsorship exclusively concerned Visma-Lease a Bike's women's team, so as it stands, a new title sponsor for the men's team is still unknown. That means that the two squads will have different names for the first time, having shared names since the women's team launched in 2021. "Given our shared history, the return of the Rabobank name as a title partner is a special moment," said Visma-Lease a Bike CEO Richard Plugge."It demonstrates Rabobank’s confidence in our team and in the future of women’s cycling. We are proud to build on that confidence together."Remarkably, the team’s two star riders will be pulling on Rabobank-emblazoned jerseys once more, with both Marianne Vos and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot having ridden for the former Rabobank-sponsored women’s team (a separate team to the men’s) during the bank’s five sponsorship years from 2012 to 2016.Rabobank’s tumultuous relationship with pro cyclingRabobank’s association with cycling stretches back to 1996, when it began its long-running title sponsorship of the men’s team that is now known as Visma-Lease a Bike. The team was one of the most prominent forces in the men’s peloton throughout the quarter of a century that Rabobank sponsored the team, and it is again now, but there was a fallow period when the Dutch bank withdrew at the end of 2012.The US Anti-Doping Agency’s landmark 2012 report into doping by Lance Armstrong and others had recently been published, and Rabobank publicly stated it had lost faith that men’s cycling could be a clean sport, though it did continue its title sponsorship of the women’s team for another four seasons.And they were highly successful seasons, with Vos enjoying the most prolific years of her extraordinary career as a Rabobank rider. She and Ferrand-Prévot kept the elite women’s road race rainbow jersey within the team for three years – Vos winning back-to-back world titles in 2012 and 2013, followed by Ferrand-Prévot in 2014. It was a similar story in cyclo-cross, with Vos winning the world title in 2012, 2013, and 2014, and Ferrand-Prévot winning it in 2015.Rabobank withdrew its sponsorship at the end of 2016, at which point Ferrand-Prévot moved to Canyon-SRAM, while Vos stayed as the team became WM3, Waowdeals, and CCC-Liv, leaving three years before it merged with the current LIV-AlUla-Jayco team to join this current team on its 2021 launch as Jumbo-Visma Women.Rabobank faded from view, but in recent years it has shown a willingness to return to cycling, and to pro cycling. In 2025, it returned to the Visma-Lease a Bike team as a minor sponsor, and its logo has adorned the jersey of the men’s and women’s squads since July of last year. It was recently announced that Rabobank will be the title sponsor of the NXT Classic race.On top of that, since last year it has been the title sponsor of the Rabo Dikke Banden Races, which are youth participation events in the Netherlands."When we returned to cycling last year, our ambition was to give the sport a boost, with a focus on elite sport, talent development and grassroots sport in the Netherlands," said Rabobank board member Carlo van Kemenade."Our return generated a great deal of positivity and enthusiasm. By taking on a greater role in women’s cycling, we are building on that momentum. This reflects who we are as a cooperative bank and our commitment to local communities."From the first introduction to the sport to competing at the highest level, we want to contribute to a sport in which talent has even more opportunities to flourish. For us, that is the power of investing in sport together."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Yankees 2026 Roster Report Cards: Carlos Rodón
item.author: Jonathan Farrar
item.content:encoded: Of all the pitchers on the Yankees’ roster, Carlos Rodón was the hardest for me to grade. His traditional numbers, a 7-3 record, 2.67 ERA, and 91 strikeouts, look great in the context of playing only half a season. However, he’s paid like an ace, with a $27 million average annual value, just a quarter million less than Max Fried, and only pitched half a season. The metrics tell a story of a pitcher who ground through the year despite finishing with a dazzling ERA. I was on the low end of the Pinstripe Alley staff, personally issuing a B. The staff average ended up giving the veteran an A-minus, or, as I like to think of it in this situation, an “Ace Light.” 16 games (16 GS), 84.1 IP, 2.67 ERA (158 ERA+), 3.44 FIP, 26.8 K%, 11.2 BB%, 1.8 fWAR, 2.2 rWAR, 7–3 record $27 million salary (six-year, $162 million contract); full no-trade clause; free agent in 2029Rodón’s 2026 season really got underway in October 2025, when he underwent surgery to remove loose bodies and shave down a bone spur in his left elbow. This caused Rodón to miss spring training and the first six weeks of the 2026 regular season. The team activated Rodón from the 15-day injured list on May 10th to officially start his 2026 season.As one would expect, Rodón was rusty initially, and his command was off, to the tune of a 16.0 percent walk rate in May. Rodón needed 354 pitches just to record his first 19 innings of work on the season as he worked on his mechanics and tried to find a consistent release point. He looked better in June but was still issuing free passes at a high rate. Pretty much every start seemed to be a grind, resulting in six innings or fewer and around three earned runs. At the end of June, Rodón’s left elbow flared up and landed him on the shelf. This first stint of his season ended with a 4-2 record and 3.30 ERA across 46.1 innings.It was not until mid-August that Rodón would return. He made three starts over the rest of the month, and his command looked a lot better. From the first stint to the second, his walk rate was cut nearly in half, from 13.4% before the IL stint (26 BB in 194 TBF) to 8.2% after his return (12 BB in 146 TBF).The old lefty saved his best for last. In September, over his final four starts, Rodón went 3-0 with a 1.42 ERA, 0.75 WHIP, 28 strikeouts, and just seven walks across 25.1 innings. Opponents hit just .141 off him during this stretch. The cherry on top was the eight scoreless innings he pitched against the Rays on September 22, which ended up being his final appearance of the season. This win gave him number 100 and he collected strikeout number 1,500 for his career. In this second act of the season he went 3-1 with a 1.89 ERA across 38.0 innings. Now, if you’re like me, after seeing all that positive, you might be thinking, that’s not the pitcher I remember watching. That could be due to nearly every underlying indicator suggesting Rodón should have been giving up more runs. Over a larger sample, predictive models peg his true performance closer to the mid-3.00s in ERA (3.29 xERA, 3.44 FIP, 3.73 xFIP, and 4.61 botERA).Rodón also benefited from some favorable batted-ball results in 2026, posting a .220 BABIP that ranked in the 98th percentile and sat roughly 70 points below league average. There was also a big 50-point gap between opponents’ actual .254 wOBA and their .304 xwOBA, suggesting that hitters were not getting the results their contact quality might have warranted. To his credit, Rodón kept the ball in the yard this season, allowing just 0.75 HR/9, and that elite mark, especially for a fly ball pitcher, helped his numbers significantly. Rodón lost command at times, contributing to some difficult innings, but he also found ways to limit the damage and keep opponents off the scoreboard. He did not allow more than three runs in any start and yet only registered six quality starts on the year. Rodón’s 2026 season had a dash of batted-ball luck, a run down the stretch where he looked like an ace, and underlying peripherals that look more like those of a solid third option. One last little nugget: Rodón was the Yankees’ Roberto Clemente Award nominee for the second straight season, a commendation on his terrific philanthropic efforts through the foundation he runs with his wife, Ashley. Here’s to hoping 2027 brings a year of health and a continuation of outperforming computer projections.See more of the Yankees Roster Report Card series here.

item.title: Bezzecchi denies Marquez top spot in overshadowed practice
item.author: Eden Hannigan
item.content:encoded: Marquez produced a pre-prepared slideshow on cards with a statement before the start of FP1, announcing that the Valencian Grand Prix will be his last weekend as a MotoGP rider. The rest of the action on track paled in comparison to the talk off track, with the speculation increasing over Ducati's future line-up following the bombshell announcement. However, Bezzecchi took matters into his own hands with the on-track action, as he set a 1m30.681s.With Bezzecchi still hunting team-mate Aprilia Jorge Martin for second in the championship, he started off his weekend strongly at a track where he won in 2025. Marquez was a close second, just 0.010 seconds off top spot amid the heavy attention on him after the breaking news. Trackhouse Aprilia’s Raul Fernandez completed the top three ahead of Gresini Ducati pair Fermin Aldeguer and Alex Marquez.Pedro Acosta - whose 2027 at Ducati now looks pretty different - was sixth, while Johann Zarco crashed towards the end of FP1 but still took seventh over Fabio Di Giannantonio. Martin was ninth, 0.504s off team-mate Bezzecchi’s best time, as Ai Ogura completed the top 10.
