item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: Isn’t it crazy that nearly a fifth of the Knicks’ regular-season games after tonight’s matchup would have been played against the same opponent in the Cavs?Well, that’s true, and so is that New York is about to beat Cleveland to take a 2-1 series lead, won’t it?Here’s a damn whole lot of quotes to keep you entertained before tipoff.On the inconsistency of the media’s coverage and criticism of Mikal Bridges:“Yes. Yes. But that’s your guys’ [the media] job; that’s why you guys get paid. You guys get paid to question and embellish and some other things. We understand that; we know it. You’re looking for stories; we know it.”On Cleveland’s physicality and what the Knicks must improve in their third meeting Wednesday:“They were real physical in Game 2. You give them credit. They talked about keeping us off the glass and some other things, and they did it. They’re a great-coached team with Kenny Atkinson and a great team in general.“There’s gonna have to be a lot of things that we do better in this game, starting with the level of physicality, while getting out in transition, if we expect to get a win.”On using Jose Alvarado alongside Jalen Brunson to relieve defensive pressure:“To be able to get (Brunson) off the ball and let somebody else handle the pressure has been huge for us. And also, it gives (Brunson’s) defender a different rhythm, as opposed to being on the ball from the start to the end. You can get in a certain rhythm and get locked in pretty good with it. It can be to your advantage, but if he’s on the ball, then off the ball, then back on the ball, that’s a little harder to adjust to.”On drawing inspiration from how Golden State deployed Stephen Curry:“I’m not comparing the players at all in terms of their game, but when I was in Golden State, we used Steph (Curry this way). He was on the ball, then he was off the ball, and to have to make that adjustment throughout the course of the game, not just once or twice but multiple times, is huge. And Jose gives us that ability, because he can guard certain players on the other team, and then if you wanna pressure him, he’s been in that position before. He’ll go by you and sometimes still execute our offense, but he can go by you and make you pay with sprays.”On his preseason conversation with Jose Alvarado and Tyler Kolek about competing for minutes:“I said, ‘Hey, right now, Jose, it’s your job because you finished the season that way and you both helped us win at a high level.’ ‘Tyler, you helped us win the NBA Cup and Jose, you helped us win in the finals.’ And I said you guys are really close and it may be you, Jose, for seven games and then it could be Tyler for three, so it’s going to be a competition you have to be ready for the entire year.”On Alvarado’s defensive advantages over Kolek and the latter’s development:“Jose Alvarado gives us that ability because he can guard certain players on the other team. And then if you want to pressure him he’s been in that position before, he’ll go by you and sometimes still execute our offense, but he can go by you and make you pay with sprays.“Tyler Kolek has been getting better on the defensive end of the floor. He’s improved a lot and he’s going to continue to improve as a young guy but Jose has been in the league longer and he knows the league, a little quicker. Teams don’t try and attack him in an iso situation because, as quick as he is, if you mess around with the ball too much he may get a steal and go the other way with it.”On the Alvarado-Brunson pairing not being exclusively reserved for closing games:“Well it’s not closing moments. It’s just throughout the course of the ballgame, it’s slotted on my minute sheet and if you think back, the probably best game that comes to mind is in Indiana. Even in the first [of two games last week] in Toronto teams are picking up trying to wear him down and so to be able to get him off the ball and let somebody else handle pressure has been huge for us.“Also, it gives his defender a different rhythm as opposed to being on the ball from the start to the end. You can get in a certain rhythm and get locked in pretty good with it and it can be to your advantage but if he’s on the ball then off the ball then back on the ball that’s a little harder to adjust to.”On Josh Hart’s triple-double and defensive performance against Indiana:“Josh, triple-double. He was really good tonight on both ends of the floor. He was our defensive player of the game, so just a whale of a game for him.”On Landry Shamet’s season to date:“He should be sixth man of the year. It’s not even close.”On identifying with Knicks fans:“I always see myself in the fans. I look in the crowd, and I see 19,000 people that look just like me.”On Knicks fans pulling over on the highway in the Hamptons to take pictures with him:“I was just with my family. I forgot what we were doing. We were doing something and it was, like, three, four or five cars that’s driving, pulling over to ask for photos. I’m like, bro, I ain’t one of these [superstars]. I ain’t KD. I ain’t Bron. I ain’t Steph. But for that it was funny because I’m just like, that shows you the love and the appreciation that New York Knicks fans have, to be on the highway and pull over and ask me for a photo. Whether you’re in New York, the Hamptons or any vacation spot that real New Yorkers go to, you get the love and the appreciation. It’s cool because you’re able to see what the actual heartbeat of the Garden is.”On the image that comes to mind when thinking about hardworking New Yorkers:On seeing his own sacrifices and work ethic reflected in Knicks fans:“When people ask me about it, I always say I see myself in the fans because at the end of the day, well, yeah, I’m probably a little more athletic than they are, a little more gifted in terms of basketball than they are, but New York is hard work. It’s a lot of countless hours, a lot of loss, you know, losing sleep, a lot of sacrifice. And I feel like it’s the same in my shoes, and that’s when I go out and play as hard as I can, because I look in the crowd and I see 19,000 people that look just like me. I think that’s what New Yorkers look like.”On finding consistency in New York under Tom Thibodeau:“I felt like I had moments in L.A. and New Orleans and Portland. But I feel like once I got to New York, starting with Thibs, it was a constant.”On his unpredictable playing style and approaching NBA games like playground basketball:“I feel like sometimes that’s why a scouting report might be tough for someone like me because it’s just, like, you don’t know what he’s gonna do this day. You don’t know if he might hit four or five threes today or he might have 2 points but 15 rebounds or he might have 6, 7 assists. If you go to a park right now and you just see a kid playing and just doing random stuff, that’s JHart, and that’s how I look at it when I step on the court. I look back to when I’m playing in the playground, I’m just doing random stuff. But it’s random stuff within somewhat of a structure.”On prioritizing his teammates’ success over his own:“I don’t really play the game for praise or anything like that. I’ll leave that. I want JB to get his flowers, KAT, Kal, OG, Deuce, Lan. I want those guys to get their flowers, and if I get it, cool. But that’s more important to me, seeing those guys get the accolades that they want, the contracts that they want, the money that they want, the notoriety that they want. And if they get that and I don’t get any, I’m cool with it. So I don’t know, I just… I feel like it changed. I feel like before, you know, you wanted the glitz and the glamour about it, but I don’t know. It’s not really in my heart anymore.”On unrealistic expectations surrounding Bridges because of the Knicks’ trade package:“Everyone looks at the trade package and they expect him to be like a No. 2 guy, No. 3 guy, but that’s not what is asked of him to do. He was a guy who was the No. 1 option in Brooklyn. I’m not sure what it was, but I’m sure he was probably averaging around 20 [points per game] or close to it. We got him and we basically asked him to take a smaller role. So you’re not necessarily gonna get the production of a 1A guy being the fourth option, the fifth option at times.”On Bridges sacrificing individual production for the team’s success:“I think it’s unfair in that regard, because he could do more, and I’m sure at times he wants to do more, but he’s willing to sacrifice and put the team in front of himself, which we commend him for. … His role could be bigger. I’m sure he at times would like it to be bigger. But he never says anything about it, he never mopes around about it. He just does what is asked of him to do and he tries to do it to the best of his ability.”On passing up easy baskets to give others scoring opportunities:“I don’t play the game for stats. I just saw an open man in front of me. Kind of the same thing in Toronto where it was a bobbled play; I could have went and got a dunk and tried to get going offensively. But see a guy in front of me, I’m going to pass it.”On Brunson returning a pass to help him overcome his physical and mental struggles during recent games“Oh yeah, for sure. That shows, obviously, he knows I’ve been struggling a little bit physically and mentally and trying to figure it out and trying to get there, that was one of the things, get that pass, get an easy two points, see the ball go through and then play.”On climbing the Knicks’ all-time triple-double leaderboard and late improvement:“I don’t know. It feels good to be stacking up some good games. I feel like the last couple games have been better. I have been knocking down shots, but the quality of my play has been better. Obviously, it feels good to have three games in a row that have been better. It feels good that I continue to stack them.”On dealing with a lingering injury to his shooting shoulder:“A lot of things are going on with my shoulder. It’s been barking for a couple weeks. So now, we got a couple days where we can figure some stuff out within the couple-day break and hopefully get it feeling better.”On whether his shoulder injury is affecting his shooting:On whether Taylor Swift is welcome at Madison Square Garden:“Obviously. I can’t believe I have to say this. But I didn’t say what was said. Being one of the leaders of the team — the captain of the team — I guess I now have to help somebody out. Yes, she’s a member of the Knicks fandom. Yes, she is.”On outside narratives surrounding Bridges and his work ethic:“Everyone outside this organization has their own narrative or belief in things that we can do as a team or players can do individually. But that’s just their own narrative. … He’s one of the hardest workers we have and that won’t change.”On Bridges’ ability to deliver in high-pressure situations:“We’ve seen what he does when the lights are the brightest. He steps up to the plate. Mikal’s one of those guys, when you have him in the locker room, when he’s on your team, you feel really good about your odds.”On what makes Alvarado such a difficult opponent:“It’s annoying. Any person on the other team will tell you the same thing. He’s a pest. Obviously, you see him shooting the ball really well these last two games. When he’s bringing his whole arsenal to the game, he’s a dangerous player for any team.”On Bridges’ character, work ethic and ability to handle outside criticism:“He’s one of the best people I know. I get the pleasure of seeing him every day and seeing how he works. Knowing that any good and bad stretch in the NBA can change very quickly, he’s always in a position to put himself in a good position and keep himself there. He knows what he’s capable of, I know what he’s capable of, and he’s always gonna do the right thing, take care of his teammates and take care of the work on his end, which is to keep fighting, regardless of noise — and there’s a lot of it that he has to deal with. He does a hell of a job.”On repeatedly rewatching Game 4 of the NBA Finals throughout the summer:“It obviously made it 10 times better that I was a part of it. But that was my favorite game watching as a fan.”On not considering himself a small guard and earning Brown’s defensive trust:“(I) don’t play like that. I think Mike believes in me defensively and understands that I can definitely play a bigger point guard role.”On the Knicks’ mutual trust despite competition for playing time:“Yeah, I mean we just trust everybody on the roster. You never know when your number is going to be called, so we just got to be ready. And we’re big on that, you know, just trust each other, and whoever is out there, we believe they’re going to win the game.“I mean, it showed from last year. If you look at how we celebrated when we were winning and you know certain people, certain roles, were doing what they were supposed to do and we just had to cheer them on — genuinely. We really care about each other, and we know whoever’s name is out there, we’re going to just believe in whoever is out there and win the game.”

item.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
item.author: Tom Wilson, Financial Times
item.content:encoded: Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command.

item.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
item.author: Dan Kagan-Kans, Understanding AI
item.content:encoded: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics.LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online.The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI.

item.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: The missions affected by the outageshopefully temporaryare NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001 and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.author: Jonathan Wilson
item.content:encoded: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoidedIn as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.author: Barry Glendenning
item.content:encoded: Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum.In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries. Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams.Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett.Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: Liverpool thrashed 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday to climb to fourth in the Premier League. But the defeat left United 19th, only one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace. There was no new manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino, who saw Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute for a last-ditch foul on Alexander Isak.Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the loss, but claimed the dismissal was wrong and United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. item.author: Andy Hunter at Anfield
item.content:encoded: Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again.Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liverpool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s Premier League history.Continue reading...
